<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
  <title>Grave Shift</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:," />
  <!-- Both typefaces are self-hosted in vendor/fonts. Same two faces the game always
       used; they came off fonts.googleapis.com, which meant the first paint waited on a
       third party and the game could not start offline at all. -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="vendor/fonts/fonts.css">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="ui/night-vision.css">
  <style>
    :root {
      /* Tactical field-HUD palette: dark olive glass, amber for primary actions,
         sage for secondary/safe actions, red for danger. Kept separate from the
         world's own greens so panels read as UI, not terrain. */
      --ink: #eef2e2;
      --ink-dim: #b7c2a8;
      --panel-bg: rgba(15,19,13,.66);
      --panel-bg-solid: #12160e;
      --panel-border: rgba(206,222,150,.24);
      --accent: #d8c25a;
      --accent-ink: #1c1608;
      --accent-2: #74c9ae;
      --accent-2-ink: #06201a;
      --danger: #dd5b4c;
      --danger-ink: #2a0906;
      --font-display: 'Black Ops One', 'Chakra Petch', system-ui, sans-serif;
      --font-hud: 'Chakra Petch', system-ui, sans-serif;
    }
    * { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
    html, body { width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; background: #0a0d08; font-family: var(--font-hud); user-select: none; -webkit-user-select: none; }
    canvas { display: block; }
    /* Gameplay hides OS cursor; menus/buttons keep pointer via their own rules */
    body.playing, body.playing canvas, body.playing #hud { cursor: none; }
    #hud {
      position: fixed; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; z-index: 4;
      color: var(--ink); text-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.6);
    }
    #reticle {
      position: fixed; left: 0; top: 0; width: 16px; height: 16px;
      margin-left: -8px; margin-top: -8px;
      pointer-events: none; z-index: 7; display: none;
      /* soft white/cyan cross + center dot with dark outline */
      background:
        radial-gradient(circle at center, rgba(180,240,255,0.95) 0 1.6px, transparent 1.8px),
        linear-gradient(rgba(12,18,28,0.9), rgba(12,18,28,0.9)) center/16px 2px no-repeat,
        linear-gradient(rgba(12,18,28,0.9), rgba(12,18,28,0.9)) center/2px 16px no-repeat,
        linear-gradient(rgba(200,240,255,0.92), rgba(200,240,255,0.92)) center/14px 1.5px no-repeat,
        linear-gradient(rgba(200,240,255,0.92), rgba(200,240,255,0.92)) center/1.5px 14px no-repeat;
      filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.85));
    }
    /* Shot line-of-sight (see updateShotLos): green when the round would actually
       reach the zombie under the cursor, red when a trunk, rock or rise is in the
       way. The cross keeps its dark outline in both so it stays readable against
       grass and sky; only the bright strokes and the centre dot change colour. */
    #reticle.los-clear {
      background:
        radial-gradient(circle at center, rgba(150,255,170,0.98) 0 1.8px, transparent 2px),
        linear-gradient(rgba(12,18,28,0.9), rgba(12,18,28,0.9)) center/16px 2px no-repeat,
        linear-gradient(rgba(12,18,28,0.9), rgba(12,18,28,0.9)) center/2px 16px no-repeat,
        linear-gradient(rgba(120,250,150,0.95), rgba(120,250,150,0.95)) center/14px 1.5px no-repeat,
        linear-gradient(rgba(120,250,150,0.95), rgba(120,250,150,0.95)) center/1.5px 14px no-repeat;
    }
    #reticle.los-blocked {
      background:
        radial-gradient(circle at center, rgba(255,120,105,0.98) 0 1.8px, transparent 2px),
        linear-gradient(rgba(12,18,28,0.9), rgba(12,18,28,0.9)) center/16px 2px no-repeat,
        linear-gradient(rgba(12,18,28,0.9), rgba(12,18,28,0.9)) center/2px 16px no-repeat,
        linear-gradient(rgba(255,110,95,0.95), rgba(255,110,95,0.95)) center/14px 1.5px no-repeat,
        linear-gradient(rgba(255,110,95,0.95), rgba(255,110,95,0.95)) center/1.5px 14px no-repeat;
    }
    /* CU-96: four ticks at the radius of the cone the next round is thrown in, where the cursor is (--sp, set every
       frame from the same cone: wider on the move, in a burst, with a pair; tighter crouched or with the laser); a ring
       when the cursor is on a head with a clear line; an X that flashes on a hit (white), a headshot (gold), a kill (red). */
    #reticle { --sp: 7px; }
    #reticle i { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; pointer-events: none; }
    #reticle .rt { background: rgba(200,240,255,0.92); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(12,18,28,0.8); }
    #reticle .rt-u, #reticle .rt-d { width: 2px; height: 5px; margin: -2.5px 0 0 -1px; }
    #reticle .rt-l, #reticle .rt-r { width: 5px; height: 2px; margin: -1px 0 0 -2.5px; }
    #reticle .rt-u { transform: translateY(calc(-1 * var(--sp) - 2.5px)); }
    #reticle .rt-d { transform: translateY(calc(var(--sp) + 2.5px)); }
    #reticle .rt-l { transform: translateX(calc(-1 * var(--sp) - 2.5px)); }
    #reticle .rt-r { transform: translateX(calc(var(--sp) + 2.5px)); }
    #reticle.no-spread .rt { display: none; }
    #reticle.los-clear .rt { background: rgba(120,250,150,0.95); }
    #reticle.los-blocked .rt { background: rgba(255,110,95,0.95); }
    #reticle .rh { width: 11px; height: 11px; margin: -6.5px 0 0 -6.5px; border: 1.5px solid rgba(255,214,90,0.98); border-radius: 50%; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(12,18,28,0.7); display: none; }
    #reticle.los-head .rh { display: block; }
    #reticle .rx { width: 22px; height: 22px; margin: -11px 0 0 -11px; opacity: 0; color: #fff;
      background: linear-gradient(45deg, transparent 43%, currentColor 43% 57%, transparent 57%), linear-gradient(-45deg, transparent 43%, currentColor 43% 57%, transparent 57%);
      -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 0 4.5px, #000 5px); mask: radial-gradient(circle, transparent 0 4.5px, #000 5px);
      filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.9)); }
    /* Tactical panel: clipped top-right / bottom-left corners + a small accent
       tab, standing in for the old fully-rounded "glassmorphism" card. */
    .glass {
      position: relative;
      background: var(--panel-bg); border: 1px solid var(--panel-border);
      clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 12px) 0, 100% 12px, 100% 100%, 12px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 12px));
      backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
      box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.32);
    }
    .glass::before {
      content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 34px; height: 3px;
      background: var(--accent);
    }
    #hudTopLeft {
      position: absolute; top: 14px; left: 16px; width: 248px;
      padding: 12px 14px 13px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 9px;
    }
    #title {
      font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 17px; font-weight: 400;
      letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent);
      display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; line-height: 1.1;
      text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.6);
    }
    #title .badge {
      font-family: var(--font-hud); font-size: 10px; background: var(--accent-2); color: var(--accent-2-ink);
      padding: 3px 8px; border-radius: 3px; text-shadow: none;
      font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em;
    }
    #stats {
      font-size: 12px; opacity: 0.92; line-height: 1.4;
      display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px;
      font-weight: 500;
    }
    #stats .stat-row { opacity: 0.95; }
    #stats .stat-row .label { color: var(--ink-dim); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; margin-right: 3px; }
    #coins { color: var(--accent); font-weight: 700; }
    #landStat { display: none; }
    #hpBarWrap { width: 100%; }
    /* Volume sliders (pause > settings) */
    .volumes { display: flex; gap: 18px; justify-content: center; margin-top: 16px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
    .volumes label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-dim); }
    .volumes label span { min-width: 44px; text-align: right; }
    .volumes label b { min-width: 26px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink, #eee); font-weight: 600; }
    .volumes input[type=range] { width: 130px; accent-color: var(--accent, #e8b84a); cursor: pointer; }
    #hpLabel {
      font-size: 9px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase;
      color: var(--ink-dim); margin-bottom: 3px; font-weight: 600;
    }
    #hpBarBg {
      position: relative; height: 15px;
      clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 7px) 0, 100% 7px, 100% 100%, 7px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 7px));
      background: rgba(0,0,0,.55); overflow: hidden;
      border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.12);
    }
    #hpBarFill {
      height: 100%; width: 100%;
      background: linear-gradient(90deg, #b32424 0%, #d69a1f 45%, #4fae3d 100%);
      transform-origin: left center; transition: width 0.12s linear;
      position: relative;
    }
    /* Gauge ticks: a faint 10%-step overlay so the bar reads as instrumentation. */
    #hpBarBg::after {
      content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none;
      background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0,0,0,.28) 0 1px, transparent 1px 10%);
    }
    #hpNum {
      position: absolute; inset: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
      font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.04em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
      text-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.8); pointer-events: none;
    }
    #hpExtra {
      margin-top: 4px; font-size: 11px; opacity: 0.8; font-weight: 600;
      min-height: 14px; color: var(--ink-dim);
    }
    /* Armor gauge: same instrument styling as health, thinner, steel blue. Only shown
       once a piece of armour has been bought. */
    #armorBarWrap { margin-top: 5px; }
    #armorLabel {
      font-size: 9px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase;
      color: var(--ink-dim); margin-bottom: 2px; font-weight: 600;
    }
    #armorBarBg {
      position: relative; height: 11px;
      clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 5px) 0, 100% 5px, 100% 100%, 5px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 5px));
      background: rgba(0,0,0,.55); overflow: hidden;
      border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.12);
    }
    #armorBarFill {
      height: 100%; width: 100%;
      background: linear-gradient(90deg, #35607c 0%, #5d9ec4 60%, #a9dcf5 100%);
      transition: width 0.12s linear; position: relative;
    }
    #armorBarBg::after {
      content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none;
      background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0,0,0,.28) 0 1px, transparent 1px 10%);
    }
    #armorNum {
      position: absolute; inset: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
      font-size: 9px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.04em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
      text-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.8); pointer-events: none;
    }
    #armorBarWrap.empty #armorLabel { color: #c9694a; }
    #centerHud {
      position: absolute; top: 14px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%);
      display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 6px;
      pointer-events: none;
    }
    /* Kill-streak readout: fades in from the second consecutive kill, the bar under
       it is the time left to keep the chain alive. */
    #combo {
      position: absolute; top: 92px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%) scale(0.85);
      display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 2px;
      opacity: 0; transition: opacity .18s ease, transform .18s ease; pointer-events: none;
      text-align: center;
    }
    #combo.show { opacity: 1; transform: translateX(-50%) scale(1); }
    #combo.pop { transform: translateX(-50%) scale(1.22); transition: transform .06s ease; }
    #combo .n {
      font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 34px; line-height: 1; color: var(--accent);
      text-shadow: 0 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.7), 0 0 14px rgba(216,194,90,.35);
      font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
    }
    #combo .l {
      font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 700;
      color: var(--ink-dim);
    }
    #combo .m { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--accent-2); letter-spacing: 0.06em; min-height: 13px; }
    #combo .bar { width: 96px; height: 3px; background: rgba(0,0,0,.5); margin-top: 2px; overflow: hidden; }
    #combo .bar i { display: block; height: 100%; width: 100%; background: var(--accent); transform-origin: left center; }
    #combo.hot .n { color: #ff8a3c; text-shadow: 0 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.7), 0 0 18px rgba(255,138,60,.55); }
    #combo.hot .bar i { background: #ff8a3c; }
    /* Headshot ping: rides just above the reticle, snaps in, drifts up and fades. */
    #hitPing {
      position: fixed; left: 0; top: 0; pointer-events: none; z-index: 5;
      font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #ffd24a;
      text-shadow: 0 1px 0 #000, 0 0 10px rgba(255,210,74,.6);
      opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, -34px) scale(0.7);
      transition: opacity .35s ease-out, transform .35s ease-out;
    }
    #hitPing.on { opacity: 1; transform: translate(-50%, -44px) scale(1); transition: opacity .05s, transform .08s cubic-bezier(.2,1.6,.4,1); }
    #ammo {
      position: absolute; bottom: 18px; left: 16px;
      display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px;
      padding: 10px 16px 10px 14px; min-width: 200px; max-width: 46vw;
    }
    #ammoCount {
      font-family: var(--font-hud); font-size: 30px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em;
      line-height: 1; min-width: 1.5em; text-align: center; color: var(--accent);
      font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
    }
    #ammoMeta { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
    #ammoWeapon { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; }
    #ammoDetail { font-size: 11px; opacity: 0.82; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
    #grenadeChips { display: flex; gap: 4px; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; }
    .gchip {
      font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; padding: 3px 7px; border-radius: 3px;
      background: rgba(116,201,174,.16); border: 1px solid rgba(116,201,174,.4);
      color: var(--accent-2); letter-spacing: 0.04em;
    }
    /* Empty-magazine prompt. The ammo panel turning red in the bottom-left corner is
       easy to miss with a horde on you, so this sits just under the middle of the
       screen where you are already looking. */
    #reloadPrompt {
      position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 58%; transform: translateX(-50%);
      display: none; padding: 5px 14px;
      font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase;
      color: #ffd24a; background: rgba(12,18,28,.62);
      border: 1px solid rgba(255,210,74,.5);
      clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 8px) 0, 100% 8px, 100% 100%, 8px 100%, 0 calc(100% - 8px));
      text-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.8);
      animation: reloadPulse 0.85s ease-in-out infinite;
    }
    #reloadPrompt.show { display: block; }
    #reloadPrompt.dry { color: #ff9282; border-color: rgba(255,146,130,.55); }
    @keyframes reloadPulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.42; } }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { #reloadPrompt { animation: none; } }
    /* Radial wheels (hold Q / hold B). A real segmented ring: wedges drawn as SVG
       arcs around a hub, one icon per wedge, the selected one reaching further out
       and lit. Wedge geometry is generated from the slot count, so a 10-slot
       weapon ring and an 11-slot build ring are both exactly symmetrical without
       anyone hand-placing anything. */
    #wheel { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: none; z-index: 6; pointer-events: none; }
    #wheel.show { display: block; }
    #wheelDim {
      position: absolute; inset: 0;
      background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, rgba(5,7,4,.16) 0 20%, rgba(5,7,4,.70) 62%);
    }
    #wheelStage {
      position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; width: 470px; height: 470px;
      margin: -235px 0 0 -235px;
    }
    #wheelSvg { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: visible; }
    .wSeg {
      fill: rgba(10,15,22,.80); stroke: rgba(190,215,240,.13); stroke-width: 1;
      transition: fill .07s linear, stroke .07s linear;
    }
    .wSeg.sel { fill: rgba(255,210,74,.20); stroke: rgba(255,210,74,.85); stroke-width: 1.4; }
    .wSeg.locked { fill: rgba(10,15,22,.55); }
    .wSeg.locked.sel { fill: rgba(255,179,71,.16); stroke: rgba(255,179,71,.8); }
    .wIcon { fill: rgba(226,238,250,.80); transition: fill .07s linear; pointer-events: none; }
    .wIcon.sel { fill: var(--accent); }
    .wIcon.locked { fill: rgba(226,238,250,.26); }
    .wIcon.locked.sel { fill: #ffb347; }
    #wheelHub {
      position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
      width: 158px; text-align: center; pointer-events: none;
    }
    #wheelHubName {
      font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 18px; letter-spacing: .04em;
      line-height: 1.1; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent);
    }
    #wheelHubMeta {
      font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; opacity: .85; margin-top: 5px; line-height: 1.3;
      font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
    }
    /* CL-113: unarmed is the hub; chosen, it lights like a wedge. */
    #wheelHub.unarmed::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; width: 160px; height: 160px; margin: -80px 0 0 -80px;
      border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(255,210,74,.22), rgba(255,210,74,.05) 70%, transparent 72%); z-index: -1; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .wSeg, .wIcon, .wNum { transition: none; } }
    #ammo.empty { color: #ff9282; }
    #ammo.empty #ammoCount { color: #ff9282; }
    #ammo.empty .gchip { border-color: rgba(255,138,122,.45); background: rgba(255,80,60,.14); }
    #modeSelect, #win, #pause {
      display: none; position: absolute; inset: 0; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
      background: rgba(5,7,4,.76); pointer-events: auto; z-index: 5;
    }
    #modeSelect.show, #win.show, #pause.show { display: flex; }
    #modeSelect.credits-open .menu-content { display: none; }
    #menuCredits { display: none; position: relative; z-index: 1; width: min(620px, 86vw); max-height: min(82vh, 680px); overflow-y: auto; padding: 24px 28px; border-left: 2px solid #a84b3d; background: rgba(6, 12, 9, .9); color: #d5d9cb; }
    #modeSelect.credits-open #menuCredits { display: block; }
    .game-version { margin-left: 14px; opacity: 0.55; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.12em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
    .game-version:empty { display: none; }
    #menuCredits h2 { font-size: clamp(28px, 5vw, 46px); margin: 0 0 18px; }
    #menuCredits dl { margin: 0; }
    #menuCredits dt { margin-top: 18px; color: #a7b49c; font: 700 11px var(--font-hud); letter-spacing: .16em; text-transform: uppercase; }
    #menuCredits dd { margin: 5px 0 0; font: 16px/1.45 var(--font-hud); }
    #menuCreditsBack { margin-top: 24px; }
    @media (max-width: 600px) { #menuCredits { box-sizing: border-box; width: 88vw; max-height: 78vh; padding: 20px; } #menuCredits dd { font-size: 14px; } }
    #nameRow { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; margin: 2px 0 14px; text-align: left; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink-dim); }
    #playerName { pointer-events: auto; font-family: var(--font-hud); font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .04em; padding: 10px 12px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.06); border: 1px solid var(--panel-border); color: var(--ink); outline: none; user-select: text; -webkit-user-select: text; }
    #playerName:focus { border-color: var(--accent); background: rgba(255,255,255,.1); }
    /* Death cinematic: letterbox, a fade, a caption; the HUD steps aside. */
    #cine { position: fixed; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; z-index: 4; display: none; }
    body.cine #cine { display: block; }
    #cine .fade { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #000; opacity: 0; }
    #cine .bar { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; height: 0; background: #000; transition: height 1s ease; }
    #cine .bar.top { top: 0; } #cine .bar.bot { bottom: 0; }
    body.cinebars #cine .bar { height: 9vh; }
    /* CL-49/50/51: the loop's own cinematics (the last kill, the alarm, the morning). */
    #loopCine { position: fixed; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; z-index: 59; }
    #loopCine .bar { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; height: 0; background: #000; transition: height .28s ease; }
    #loopCine .bar.top { top: 0; } #loopCine .bar.bot { bottom: 0; }
    body.loopcine #loopCine .bar { height: 8vh; }
    #loopCine .grade { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: #7a7a7a; mix-blend-mode: saturation; opacity: 0; transition: opacity .45s ease; }
    /* CL-55 (CU-39): the grade was a grey layer with mix-blend-mode: saturation. On Jerry's
       machine the blend did not happen, so it was just a 90% grey sheet over the shot: the
       washed-out, milky finisher. It is a filter on the game canvas now (as the NVG is). */
    #loopCine .grade { display: none; }
    canvas.fin-grade:not(.nvg-phosphor) { filter: saturate(.4) contrast(1.16); }
    #loopCine .glare { position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0; background: radial-gradient(ellipse at 70% 40%, rgba(255,236,190,.95) 0%, rgba(255,210,150,.7) 45%, rgba(255,190,120,.35) 100%); }
    #loopCine .blink { position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0; background: #000; }
    body.loopcine #hud > *:not(#win):not(#bigBanner):not(#pause):not(#shop), body.loopcine #reticle, body.loopcine #hitPing { visibility: hidden !important; }

      position: fixed; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; z-index: 6; opacity: 0;
      background:
        /* center pip */
        radial-gradient(circle at center, rgba(220,255,230,0.95) 0 1.6px, transparent 2px) center/100% 100% no-repeat,
        /* crosshair, reaching from the lens edge to just short of the pip */

        linear-gradient(rgba(220,255,230,0.85), rgba(220,255,230,0.85)) center/72% 2px no-repeat,

        radial-gradient(circle at center, rgba(220,255,230,0.7) 0 1.4px, transparent 1.6px) center calc(50% - 90px)/8px 8px no-repeat,
        radial-gradient(circle at center, rgba(220,255,230,0.7) 0 1.4px, transparent 1.6px) center calc(50% + 90px)/8px 8px no-repeat,
        radial-gradient(circle at center, rgba(220,255,230,0.7) 0 1.4px, transparent 1.6px) calc(50% - 90px) center/8px 8px no-repeat,

    (() => {

      const prevTime = worldTime;
      worldTime = advanceSkyClock(dt);
      // Quarter-turn offset so the clock agrees with the sky: 00:00 midnight, 06:00
      // sunrise, 12:00 overhead, 18:00 sunset. Without it "noon" landed at dusk.
      const ang = (worldTime - 0.25) * Math.PI * 2;
      const dayFactor = Math.max(0, Math.sin(ang));
      const naturalNight = dayFactor < NIGHT_DAY_FACTOR;

      // Advance match / dawn clocks in game hours
      if (matchClockRunning) {
        const dHours = ((worldTime - prevTime + 1) % 1) * 24;
        hoursSinceMatchStart += dHours;
        hoursSinceDawn += dHours;
      }

      // Dawn detect: leave natural night into day → reset daytime grace
      if (wasNaturalNight && !naturalNight) {
        hoursSinceDawn = 0;
      }
      wasNaturalNight = naturalNight;

      // In a match the loop decides when it's night (CL-45), so the old dawn grace only
      // applies to the free-running title clock.
      const nightAllowed = skyLoop.mode !== 'free' || hoursSinceDawn >= DAWN_GRACE_HOURS;
      isNight = naturalNight && nightAllowed;
      // CU-109: the Training Ground switch is night for the flashlight and the goggles,
      // including during the dawn grace, which otherwise keeps a midnight clock in daylight.
      if (training.active && training.lightsOff) isNight = true;

      const skyDay = new THREE.Color(0x87b7ff);
      const skyDusk = new THREE.Color(0xc47a4a);
      // Near black-blue when night is active without NVG
      const skyNight = new THREE.Color(0x020508);
      let sky;
      // Lighting follows natural curve; when night blocked by grace, keep dusk-ish day
      const lightNight = isNight;
      const visualFactor = lightNight ? dayFactor : Math.max(dayFactor, NIGHT_DAY_FACTOR);
      const nvgActive = lightNight && nvgDown;
      nightReadK = lightNight && !nvgActive ? 1 - Math.min(1, dayFactor / Math.max(0.001, NIGHT_DAY_FACTOR)) : 0;   // CL-83
      if (visualFactor > 0.55) sky = skyDay.clone();
      else if (visualFactor > 0.28) sky = skyDusk.clone().lerp(skyDay, (visualFactor - 0.28) / 0.27);
      else sky = skyNight.clone().lerp(skyDusk, visualFactor / 0.28);
      if (hurtFlash <= 0 && !nvgActive) {
        (scene.background || (scene.background = SCENE_BG)).copy(sky);   // CL-138
        scene.fog.color.copy(sky);
      }
      if (lightNight && !nvgActive) {
        // Scary dark — struggle to see zombies/terrain without N
        const nightAmt = 1 - Math.min(1, dayFactor / Math.max(0.001, NIGHT_DAY_FACTOR));
        const twilight = 1 - nightAmt;
        // Meet the daytime values exactly at dusk; avoid the old sudden blackout.
        sun.intensity = 0.025 + twilight * (0.18 + NIGHT_DAY_FACTOR * 1.55 - 0.025);
        hemi.intensity = 0.15 + twilight * (0.18 + NIGHT_DAY_FACTOR * 0.5 - 0.15);
        ambientFill.intensity = 0.06 - twilight * 0.02;
        moon.intensity = 0.4 - twilight * 0.35;
        scene.fog.near = 18 + twilight * 172;
        scene.fog.far = 65 + twilight * 575;
      } else if (lightNight && nvgActive) {
        // Base night still dark; NVG boost applied in updateNvgVisual
        sun.intensity = 0.04;
        hemi.intensity = 0.18;
        ambientFill.intensity = 0.08;
        moon.intensity = 0.38;
        scene.fog.near = 50;
        scene.fog.far = 160;
      } else {
        // More sun, less fill. A strong hemisphere light washes out every slope, which
        // is what made the new landform read flat.
        sun.intensity = 0.18 + visualFactor * 1.55;
        hemi.intensity = 0.18 + visualFactor * 0.5;
        moon.intensity = 0.05;
        ambientFill.intensity = 0.04;
        // Wide enough to show the ridgeline; haze still stacks up over distance.
        scene.fog.near = 190;
        scene.fog.far = 640;
      }
      sun.color.setRGB(1, 0.74 + Math.min(1, visualFactor / 0.6) * 0.24, 0.53 + Math.min(1, visualFactor / 0.6) * 0.43);
      sunDir.set(Math.cos(ang), Math.max(0.35, Math.sin(ang)), 0.3).normalize();

      // Drive the sky dome from the same cycle so the painted sun sits where the light
      // is actually coming from, and the dome tints with the ground.
      {
        const nightMix = 1 - Math.min(1, visualFactor / 0.42);
        // CL-49: the painted sun goes down under the horizon (the light itself keeps its floor
        // of 0.35 so shadows never go flat), so the alarm's shot can watch it set.
        skyUniforms.uSunDir.value.set(Math.cos(ang), Math.max(-0.3, Math.sin(ang)), 0.3).normalize();
        // Moon rides opposite the sun.
        skyUniforms.uMoonDir.value.set(-Math.cos(ang), Math.max(0.2, -Math.sin(ang) * 0.6 + 0.45), -0.3).normalize();
        skyUniforms.uNight.value = nvgActive ? 0.25 : nightMix;
        const dusk = Math.max(0, 1 - Math.abs(visualFactor - 0.34) / 0.3);
        skyUniforms.uHorizon.value.setHex(0xd8e8ff).lerp(SKY_DUSK_LOW, dusk).lerp(SKY_NIGHT_LOW, nightMix);
        skyUniforms.uMid.value.setHex(0x87b7ff).lerp(SKY_DUSK_MID, dusk * 0.8).lerp(SKY_NIGHT_MID, nightMix);
        if (bloodMoon) {
          skyUniforms.uHorizon.value.lerp(SKY_BLOOD_LOW, nightMix * 0.85);
          skyUniforms.uMid.value.lerp(SKY_BLOOD_MID, nightMix * 0.7);
          skyUniforms.uMoonTint.value.copy(MOON_TINT_NORMAL).lerp(MOON_TINT_BLOOD, nightMix);
          moon.color.setHex(0x8899cc).lerp(new THREE.Color(0xff5a44), nightMix);
        } else {
          skyUniforms.uMoonTint.value.copy(MOON_TINT_NORMAL);
          moon.color.setHex(0x8899cc);
        }
        skyUniforms.uTop.value.setHex(0x2f6fd0).lerp(SKY_NIGHT_TOP, nightMix);
        skyUniforms.uSunTint.value.setHex(0xfff0cf).lerp(SKY_SUN_LOW, dusk);
        cloudMat.opacity = 0.8 * (0.16 + 0.84 * (1 - nightMix));
        cloudMat.emissiveIntensity = 0.22 + 0.5 * (1 - nightMix);
        cloudMat.color.setHex(0xffffff).lerp(SKY_DUSK_LOW, dusk * 0.7);
        cloudMat.emissive.setHex(0xffffff).lerp(SKY_DUSK_LOW, dusk * 0.85);
        // Distant geometry should fade into the sky it is standing against, so the fog
        // takes the dome's horizon colour rather than a separate constant.
        if (hurtFlash <= 0 && !nvgActive) scene.fog.color.copy(skyUniforms.uHorizon.value);
        // Only used if the TSL sky failed to build: keep the flat dome in step with the day.
        if (skyMat.userData && skyMat.userData.flatFallback) skyMat.color.copy(skyUniforms.uMid.value);
      }

      timeLineEl.textContent = dwText('hud.time', {period: dwText(isNight ? 'hud.night' : 'hud.day'), time: formatGameClock()}) +
        (zombieGraceActive() ? ' · ' + dwText('hud.grace') : '') + (weather.raining ? ' · ' + dwText('hud.rain') : '') + (bloodMoon ? ' · ' + dwText('hud.bloodMoon') : '');
      updateNvgVisual();
      applyFogNight(dt);   // CL-76: after the night and the goggles, so Fog Night's mist wins over both
      if (training.active) training.danger?.dim([sun, hemi, ambientFill, moon]);
      updateTacticalHud();
    }

    // CL-76 (P-57, D-54): Fog Night (night 14, GB-87's mod 'fog'). While its wave is on, the lake breathes out: a cold
    // mist closes in to about 30 m, goggles or not (it beats the NVG's wider fog, which only helps against the dark). It
    // rolls in over FOG_NIGHT.RAMP_S s at the alarm and lifts the same way at dawn. The night keeps its own sectioned
    // score (the music director already knows 'fog' as a kind; nothing changes there). fogNightForce (tests, shots)
    // overrides the plan: true, false or null.
    const FOG_NIGHT = { NEAR: 6, FAR: 32, MIST: 0x3c454b, MIST_NVG: 0x22332d, RAMP_S: 5 };
    let fogNightK = 0, fogNightForce = null, fogMistDome = null;
    const _fogMist = new THREE.Color();
    function fogNightActive() {
      if (fogNightForce != null) return !!fogNightForce;
      return phase === 'wave' && !!wavePreview && wavePreview.day === day && !!wavePreview.night && wavePreview.night.mod === 'fog';
    }
    function applyFogNight(dt) {
      const target = fogNightActive() ? 1 : 0;
      const step = Math.max(0, dt || 0) / FOG_NIGHT.RAMP_S;
      fogNightK = target > fogNightK ? Math.min(target, fogNightK + step) : Math.max(target, fogNightK - step);
      if (fogNightK <= 0 || !scene.fog) { if (fogMistDome) fogMistDome.visible = false; return; }
      const k = fogNightK * fogNightK * (3 - 2 * fogNightK);   // eased in and out
      scene.fog.near += (FOG_NIGHT.NEAR - scene.fog.near) * k;
      scene.fog.far += (FOG_NIGHT.FAR - scene.fog.far) * k;
      if (hurtFlash <= 0) {
        const goggles = nvgDown && isNight && gameStarted && !gameOver && !won;
        scene.fog.color.lerp(_fogMist.setHex(goggles ? FOG_NIGHT.MIST_NVG : FOG_NIGHT.MIST), k);
      }
      // The sky goes too: a shell of the mist's own colour round the camera, just past the fog's far edge, so the sky,
      // the clouds and the ridgeline sink into it while everything nearer stays in front of it.
      if (!fogMistDome) {
        fogMistDome = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(FOG_NIGHT.FAR + 12, 24, 14),
          new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: FOG_NIGHT.MIST, side: THREE.BackSide, transparent: true, opacity: 0, depthWrite: false, fog: false }));
        fogMistDome.name = 'fog-night-mist';
        fogMistDome.frustumCulled = false;
        scene.add(fogMistDome);
      }
      fogMistDome.visible = true;
      fogMistDome.position.copy(camera.position);
      fogMistDome.material.color.copy(scene.fog.color);
      fogMistDome.material.opacity = Math.min(1, k * 1.05);
    }

    // === Terrain (heightfield, stream, land bounds) ===
    // Map ~10× linear radius vs prior (12→120 start, 22→220 max)
    const LAND_MIN = 120;
    const LAND_MAX = 220;
    const LAND_STEP = 20;
    let landRadius = LAND_MAX; // expand disabled — full map open
    let expandLevel = 0;
    function expandCost() { return 14 + expandLevel * 12; }

    // The world extends well past the playable disc so the horizon is real geometry
    // instead of a cut-off circle. Everything beyond LAND_MAX is scenery.
    const TERRAIN_RADIUS = 430;

    // Noise, smoothing, segment distance and mulberry32 live in core/math.js.

    // --- World layout -----------------------------------------------------------
    // A lake in the south-west, fed by a river that drops out of the eastern highlands.
    const LAKE = { x: -138, z: -104, r: 58, level: -3.4 };
    // A rough "somewhere near the lake" radius, used for proximity checks only (where
    // to look for the dock's shoreline, how close you have to be to see fish rise).
    // It is NOT the water's edge: the shoreline is solved from the terrain in
    // buildWaterMask below. It used to double as the fill boundary, which is exactly
    // what went wrong — a circle drawn through a basin that reaches ~100m cut the lake
    // off mid-water and left a hard wall of it standing across open ground.
    const LAKE_FILL = LAKE.r * 1.3;
    const RIVER_WIDTH = 5.0;
    const RIVER_CTRL = [
      { x: 232, z: 132 },
      { x: 178, z: 104 },
      { x: 126, z: 84 },
      { x: 72, z: 74 },
      { x: 18, z: 70 },
      { x: -38, z: 56 },
      { x: -86, z: 24 },
      { x: -114, z: -26 },
      { x: -124, z: -72 }
    ];
    // Kept for callers that predate the rename.
    const STREAM_CTRL = RIVER_CTRL;
    const STREAM_WIDTH = RIVER_WIDTH;

    // Warped distance to the lake centre, so the shoreline has bays and spits instead
    // of being a perfect circle.
    function lakeDist(x, z) {
      const wx = x + fbm(x * 0.019 + 3.3, z * 0.019 - 1.7, 2) * 13;
      const wz = z + fbm(x * 0.019 - 5.1, z * 0.019 + 2.9, 2) * 13;
      return Math.hypot(wx - LAKE.x, wz - LAKE.z);
    }

    function distToRiver(x, z) {
      let best = Infinity;
      for (let i = 0; i < RIVER_CTRL.length - 1; i++) {
        const a = RIVER_CTRL[i], b = RIVER_CTRL[i + 1];
        const d = distPointToSeg(x, z, a.x, a.z, b.x, b.z);
        if (d < best) best = d;
      }
      return best;
    }
    const distToStream = distToRiver;

    // Cumulative arc length per control point, so a position along the river maps to a
    // bed height.
    const RIVER_ARC = [0];
    for (let i = 1; i < RIVER_CTRL.length; i++) {
      const a = RIVER_CTRL[i - 1], b = RIVER_CTRL[i];
      RIVER_ARC.push(RIVER_ARC[i - 1] + Math.hypot(b.x - a.x, b.z - a.z));
    }
    const RIVER_LEN = RIVER_ARC[RIVER_ARC.length - 1];
    const riverBed = new Float32Array(RIVER_CTRL.length);

    // Where along the river (0..1) the closest point lies, plus the distance to it.
    function riverProject(x, z) {
      let bestD = Infinity, bestS = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < RIVER_CTRL.length - 1; i++) {
        const a = RIVER_CTRL[i], b = RIVER_CTRL[i + 1];
        const abx = b.x - a.x, abz = b.z - a.z;
        const ab2 = abx * abx + abz * abz || 1e-8;
        let t = ((x - a.x) * abx + (z - a.z) * abz) / ab2;
        t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, t));
        const qx = a.x + abx * t, qz = a.z + abz * t;
        const d = Math.hypot(x - qx, z - qz);
        if (d < bestD) {
          bestD = d;
          bestS = (RIVER_ARC[i] + t * (RIVER_ARC[i + 1] - RIVER_ARC[i])) / RIVER_LEN;
        }
      }
      return { d: bestD, s: bestS };
    }

    // The bed is solved per control point, then laid out densely by arc length (s is
    // an arc-length fraction everywhere else too) so the stretch where the river runs
    // into the lake can be shaped finely — see solveRiverBed.
    const RIVER_BED_N = 600;
    const riverBedDense = new Float32Array(RIVER_BED_N + 1);
    let riverBedDenseReady = false;
    // Where the lake reaches up the channel (arc fraction). From here down the river
    // surface IS the lake surface — one level, one sheet, no step between them.
    let RIVER_JOIN_S = 1;
    function riverBedAt(s) {
      s = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, s));
      if (riverBedDenseReady) {
        const f = s * RIVER_BED_N, i = Math.min(RIVER_BED_N - 1, Math.floor(f)), t = f - i;
        return riverBedDense[i] + (riverBedDense[i + 1] - riverBedDense[i]) * t;
      }
      const target = s * RIVER_LEN;
      for (let i = 0; i < RIVER_CTRL.length - 1; i++) {
        if (RIVER_ARC[i + 1] >= target || i === RIVER_CTRL.length - 2) {
          const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (target - RIVER_ARC[i]) / (RIVER_ARC[i + 1] - RIVER_ARC[i])));
          return riverBed[i] + (riverBed[i + 1] - riverBed[i]) * t;
        }
      }
      return riverBed[riverBed.length - 1];
    }
    // The river's surface: a surface-depth over its bed.
    const RIVER_DEPTH = 1.05;
    // Never below the lake it runs into: past the join it IS the lake's surface.
    function riverSurfAt(s) { return Math.max(riverBedAt(s) + RIVER_DEPTH, LAKE.level); }

    // --- Terrain composition ----------------------------------------------------
    // Layered so each piece has one job: a broad landform, ridge lines, fine detail,
    // a flattened core around spawn, and a mountain wall past the play area.
    function terrainBase(x, z) {
      const r = Math.hypot(x, z);

      // Domain warp bends every later layer, killing the grid-aligned look that plain
      // fbm has.
      const wx = x + fbm(x * 0.0042 + 11.3, z * 0.0042 - 7.1, 3) * 34;
      const wz = z + fbm(x * 0.0042 - 3.7, z * 0.0042 + 5.9, 3) * 34;

      // Broad rolling landform.
      let h = fbm(wx * 0.0072, wz * 0.0072, 5) * 12.5;

      // Ridge lines, fading in away from the middle so spawn stays open.
      const ridgeAmt = smoothBand(40, 140, r);
      const rg = ridged(wx * 0.0056 + 3.1, wz * 0.0056 - 2.4, 4);
      h += rg * rg * 15.0 * ridgeAmt;

      // Medium bumps and fine surface detail.
      h += fbm(wx * 0.021, wz * 0.021, 3) * 2.2;
      h += fbm(x * 0.052, z * 0.052, 2) * 0.55;

      // Broad basin cradling the lake so it reads as a valley, not a crater.
      const lakeD = lakeDist(x, z);
      h -= 8.5 * smoothstep01(1 - lakeD / (LAKE.r * 2.5));

      // Settle the core. Only the immediate spawn is properly level — beyond that the
      // ground keeps most of its roll so the playable bowl still has shape to it.
      const core = 1 - smoothBand(14, 62, r);
      h = h * (1 - core) + (h * 0.4 + 0.5) * core;

      // Mountain wall past the playable disc. This is the map edge — you see a horizon
      // of peaks instead of the world simply stopping. The front line wanders, so the
      // range has bays and headlands rather than being a uniform ring.
      const wallStart = Math.max(220, 232 + fbm(wx * 0.0022 + 5.5, wz * 0.0022 - 2.2, 2) * 42);
      const wall = smoothBand(wallStart, wallStart + 100, r);
      if (wall > 0) {
        const mr = ridged(wx * 0.0034 - 9.2, wz * 0.0034 + 4.6, 5);
        const peaks = Math.pow(mr, 1.5) * 135;
        h += wall * (peaks + (r - wallStart) * 0.36);
        // Snow-line crags: extra high-frequency relief up top only.
        h += wall * fbm(wx * 0.016, wz * 0.016, 3) * 8.0;
      }

      // Lake bowl.
      if (lakeD < LAKE.r) {
        const t = 1 - lakeD / LAKE.r;
        const blend = smoothstep01(t * 2.3);
        const floor = LAKE.level - 3.8 * smoothstep01(t * 1.35);
        h += (floor - h) * blend;
      }

      return h;
    }

    // River is carved after the base so its bed can be forced monotonically downhill.
    function carveRiver(x, z, h) {
      // The channel used to go from bed to bank inside one RIVER_WIDTH, which cut a
      // slot: banks averaging 35 degrees and reaching 50, near the angle where footing
      // gives out. It read as a trench gouged into the map rather than a valley the
      // water had worn. Both falloffs are now much wider — the channel eases out over
      // 2x the river's width and the valley shoulder over 5.4x — which halves the bank
      // angle (about 22 degrees typical, 34 worst) while keeping roughly a metre of
      // water in it and the banks still standing clear above the drawn ribbon.
      const bandOuter = RIVER_WIDTH * 5.4;
      const p = riverProject(x, z);
      if (p.d > bandOuter) return h;
      const bed = riverBedAt(p.s);
      // Channel floor, then a wider valley shoulder easing into the banks.
      const chan = 1 - smoothstep01(p.d / (RIVER_WIDTH * 2.0));
      const shoulder = 1 - smoothstep01(p.d / bandOuter);
      let out = h + (bed + 3.4 - h) * shoulder * 0.62;
      out = out + (bed - out) * chan;
      // Once the river has reached the lake it may only dig, never build up. Carving
      // the lake bed like an upland channel raised it into levees along the last run
      // and a round spit around the river's end — the horseshoe of land (and the boxed
      // channel inside it) that has sat at the river mouth since the start.
      const pastJoin = smoothstep01((p.s - (RIVER_JOIN_S - 0.012)) / 0.02);
      if (pastJoin > 0) out = out + (Math.min(h, out) - out) * pastJoin;
      return out;
    }

    function terrainRaw(x, z) {
      return carveRiver(x, z, terrainBase(x, z));
    }

    // Force the river to lose height from source to mouth. Without this a river carved
    // straight onto noise runs uphill wherever the terrain happens to rise.
    (function solveRiverBed() {
      let prev = Infinity;
      for (let i = 0; i < RIVER_CTRL.length; i++) {
        const c = RIVER_CTRL[i];
        const natural = terrainBase(c.x, c.z) - 1.6;
        const drop = i === 0 ? 0 : (RIVER_ARC[i] - RIVER_ARC[i - 1]) * 0.012;
        riverBed[i] = i === 0 ? natural : Math.min(natural, prev - drop);
        prev = riverBed[i];
      }
      // Mouth bed sits a full surface-depth under the lake so the river's water
      // arrives at lake level — not 0.35m above it, which left a raised ribbon
      // floating over the lake sheet (the rectangular box at the join).
      const mouth = LAKE.level - 1.05;
      if (riverBed[riverBed.length - 1] > mouth) {
        const last = riverBed.length - 1;
        const fix = riverBed[last] - mouth;
        for (let i = 0; i <= last; i++) {
          riverBed[i] -= fix * (i / last);
        }
      }
      // Lay it out densely by arc length.
      for (let k = 0; k <= RIVER_BED_N; k++) riverBedDense[k] = riverBedAt(k / RIVER_BED_N);
      // Where does the lake reach the channel? The first point down the river whose
      // banks already stand in the lake's basin, below its surface. That is where the
      // two waters meet, and it is well upstream of the last control point — the old
      // bed only reached lake level AT that last point, so for the whole stretch in
      // between the river ran a step above the lake lying right beside it: the
      // rectangular box at the join, and every patch-up since was fighting it.
      const bankOff = RIVER_WIDTH * 1.25 + 2.5;
      for (let k = 0; k <= RIVER_BED_N; k++) {
        const sk = k / RIVER_BED_N, pt = riverPointAt(sk);
        const nx = -pt.tz, nz = pt.tx;
        const lo = Math.min(terrainBase(pt.x + nx * bankOff, pt.z + nz * bankOff), terrainBase(pt.x - nx * bankOff, pt.z - nz * bankOff));
        if (lo < LAKE.level + 0.25 && lakeDist(pt.x, pt.z) < LAKE.r * 2.2) { RIVER_JOIN_S = sk; break; }
      }
      // From the join down, the bed lies a surface-depth under the lake; above it, the
      // river comes down to the lake's level over a short run of quicker water, and
      // never dips below it.
      const lakeBed = LAKE.level - RIVER_DEPTH, RAMP = 0.07;
      for (let k = 0; k <= RIVER_BED_N; k++) {
        const sk = k / RIVER_BED_N;
        let b = riverBedDense[k];
        if (sk >= RIVER_JOIN_S) b = Math.min(b, lakeBed - 0.5 * smoothstep01((sk - RIVER_JOIN_S) / 0.06));
        else {
          b = Math.max(b, lakeBed);
          const u = (sk - (RIVER_JOIN_S - RAMP)) / RAMP;
          if (u > 0) b = b + (lakeBed - b) * smoothstep01(u);
        }
        riverBedDense[k] = k > 0 ? Math.min(b, riverBedDense[k - 1]) : b;
      }
      riverBedDenseReady = true;
    })();

    // --- Cached heightfield -----------------------------------------------------
    // terrainRaw() costs ~20 noise evaluations. Gameplay samples height hundreds of
    // times a frame, so bake it once and bilinear-sample. The render mesh reads the
    // same data, which keeps what you see and what you collide with identical.
    const HF_SPACING = 1.0;
    const HF_EXTENT = 252;
    const HF_N = Math.round((HF_EXTENT * 2) / HF_SPACING) + 1;
    const heightField = new Float32Array(HF_N * HF_N);
    let heightFieldReady = false;

    function buildHeightField() {
      for (let j = 0; j < HF_N; j++) {
        const z = -HF_EXTENT + j * HF_SPACING;
        const row = j * HF_N;
        for (let i = 0; i < HF_N; i++) {
          heightField[row + i] = terrainRaw(-HF_EXTENT + i * HF_SPACING, z);
        }
      }
      heightFieldReady = true;
    }
    buildHeightField();

    // --- Flat apron around the spawn clearing -----------------------------------
    // Building on natural ground was the root of half the placement trouble: cells
    // were refused as "too rough", and a wall run stepped down a hillside instead of
    // standing as one wall. The ground you actually build on is now level out to
    // BUILD_APRON_R and blended back into the real terrain over the feather beyond,
    // so there is no cliff at the edge of it.
    // 20m: the spawn clearing and the kiosk, not the countryside. At 100m the apron
    // ran right up to the river and met the preserved channel as a sheer cut bank.
    const BUILD_APRON_R = 20;
    const BUILD_APRON_FEATHER = 28;
    (function flattenBuildApron() {
      const cx = 0, cz = 0;
      const reach = BUILD_APRON_R + BUILD_APRON_FEATHER;
      const ci = Math.round((cx + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING);
      const cj = Math.round((cz + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING);
      const target = heightField[cj * HF_N + ci];
      const i0 = Math.max(0, Math.floor((cx - reach + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING));
      const i1 = Math.min(HF_N - 1, Math.ceil((cx + reach + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING));
      const j0 = Math.max(0, Math.floor((cz - reach + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING));
      const j1 = Math.min(HF_N - 1, Math.ceil((cz + reach + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING));
      for (let j = j0; j <= j1; j++) {
        const wz = -HF_EXTENT + j * HF_SPACING;
        for (let i = i0; i <= i1; i++) {
          const wx = -HF_EXTENT + i * HF_SPACING;
          const d = Math.hypot(wx - cx, wz - cz);
          if (d > reach) continue;
          // The river channel is left alone or the apron dams it — but it has to be
          // let go of GRADUALLY. Skipping it with a hard cutoff flattened the land
          // right to the bank and then dropped straight into the untouched channel,
          // which is the cliff face in the screenshots. The apron's pull now fades out
          // over a band either side of the water, so the bank keeps its natural slope.
          const rd = distToRiver(wx, wz);
          const riverKeep = smoothstep01((rd - RIVER_WIDTH * 1.1) / 14);
          if (riverKeep <= 0) continue;
          const k = j * HF_N + i;
          const natural = heightField[k];
          const w = (d <= BUILD_APRON_R ? 1 : 1 - smoothstep01((d - BUILD_APRON_R) / BUILD_APRON_FEATHER)) * riverKeep;
          heightField[k] = natural + (target - natural) * w;
        }
      }
    })();

    let hollowFloor = null;
    // CL-115: the Training Ground (see enterTraining). Declared up here: sampleHeight reads it from the first frame.
    const training = { active: false, tg: null, copies: null, hits: 0, wake: null, panel: null, hud: null, blackout: null, rackKey: '' };
    let trainingFloor = null;
    let onHqRoof = false;
    function sampleHeight(x, z) {
      if (trainingFloor) {   // CL-115: the Training Ground's floor (and the infirmary bed while he wakes on it)
        const w = training.wake, b = training.tg && training.tg.bed;
        if (w && b) return w.rootY ?? b.y; // GP-169: recovery owns the root height through sit/plant/stand.
        const y = trainingFloor(x, z);
        if (y != null) return y;
      }
      if (hollowFloor) {
        const y = hollowFloor(x, z);
        if (y != null) return y;
      }
      if (heightFieldReady) {
        const fx = (x + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING;
        const fz = (z + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING;
        if (fx >= 0 && fz >= 0 && fx < HF_N - 1 && fz < HF_N - 1) {
          const i = fx | 0, j = fz | 0;
          const tx = fx - i, tz = fz - j;
          const k = j * HF_N + i;
          const h00 = heightField[k], h10 = heightField[k + 1];
          const h01 = heightField[k + HF_N], h11 = heightField[k + HF_N + 1];
          const a = h00 + (h10 - h00) * tx;
          const b = h01 + (h11 - h01) * tx;
          return a + (b - a) * tz;
        }
      }
      return terrainRaw(x, z);
    }

    // --- Lake extent mask -------------------------------------------------------
    // The lake used to be DRAWN as a plain circle measured straight from its centre,
    // while "am I in water?" asked a different question: a noise-warped distance
    // (worth +/-13m) against that same radius. The two disagreed in a wide ring, which
    // is why you could stand on open grass kicking up wading ripples with no water in
    // sight, and why the shoreline read as a hard polygon edge instead of a shore.
    //
    // So the extent is solved once, here, and both the mesh and every height/depth
    // query read it: a coarse grid of the basin, flood-filled out from the deepest
    // point so only water actually connected to the lake counts (an unrelated dip in
    // the ground far from the shore no longer becomes a second, disconnected slab of
    // water). The exact waterline inside a marked cell is still decided per-point by
    // the terrain, so the edge stays as sharp as the ground is.
    // How far out from the river centreline the surface ribbon reaches. Shared by the
    // mesh, the lake fill and the water test, so the drawn edge and the wet edge are
    // the same line. Declared up here because buildWaterMask below runs immediately
    // and reads it.
    const RIVER_SURF = RIVER_WIDTH * 1.25;

    const WATER_CELL = 2.0;
    // How far out the search is even allowed to look. This is a guard against a
    // pathological basin, NOT the shoreline: the ground that actually sits below the
    // lake surface runs to about 100m from the centre, so the terrain stops the fill
    // long before this does. It matters that the cap never binds — when it did (it
    // used to sit at 75m, inside the real basin) it sliced the lake off mid-body,
    // leaving a wall of water up to 3m deep ending on a hard grid-stepped line across
    // open ground. A shoreline has to be decided by the shore.
    const LAKE_REACH = 130;
    const WM_MIN_X = LAKE.x - LAKE_REACH;
    const WM_MIN_Z = LAKE.z - LAKE_REACH;
    const WM_N = Math.ceil((LAKE_REACH * 2) / WATER_CELL) + 1;
    const lakeMask = new Uint8Array(WM_N * WM_N);

    function buildWaterMask() {
      lakeMask.fill(0);
      const raw = new Uint8Array(WM_N * WM_N);
      let seed = -1, seedDepth = 0;
      for (let j = 0; j < WM_N; j++) {
        const z = WM_MIN_Z + j * WATER_CELL;
        for (let i = 0; i < WM_N; i++) {
          const x = WM_MIN_X + i * WATER_CELL;
          if (lakeDist(x, z) >= LAKE_REACH) continue;
          const d = LAKE.level - sampleHeight(x, z);
          if (d <= 0) continue;
          // The river owns its corridor. Without this the lake fill walks up the
          // carved channel and lays a flat rectangular tongue of lake water along
          // a stretch that should still be climbing river. Only the last tip of
          // the corridor (s > 0.92) may join the lake sheet, so the two meet in a
          // short overlap instead of a hard box.
          // (The river corridor is NOT cut out of it any more. The river's surface now
          // meets the lake's at the join, so where the lake reaches up the channel it
          // is simply the same water — cutting the corridor out is what left dry
          // notches and a boxed-off tongue where they meet.)
          raw[j * WM_N + i] = 1;
          if (d > seedDepth) { seedDepth = d; seed = j * WM_N + i; }
        }
      }
      if (seed < 0) return;
      // Flood fill from the deepest cell; only what it reaches is the lake.
      const queue = [seed];
      lakeMask[seed] = 1;
      for (let head = 0; head < queue.length; head++) {
        const k = queue[head];
        const i = k % WM_N, j = (k / WM_N) | 0;
        if (i > 0 && raw[k - 1] && !lakeMask[k - 1]) { lakeMask[k - 1] = 1; queue.push(k - 1); }
        if (i < WM_N - 1 && raw[k + 1] && !lakeMask[k + 1]) { lakeMask[k + 1] = 1; queue.push(k + 1); }
        if (j > 0 && raw[k - WM_N] && !lakeMask[k - WM_N]) { lakeMask[k - WM_N] = 1; queue.push(k - WM_N); }
        if (j < WM_N - 1 && raw[k + WM_N] && !lakeMask[k + WM_N]) { lakeMask[k + WM_N] = 1; queue.push(k + WM_N); }
      }
      // Hollows beside the lake that dip below its surface but are cut off from it by a
      // low ridge would hold water too — ground water, rain. Left dry they read as
      // pits dug next to the shore, so any of a decent size become ponds at the lake's
      // level (the ridge round them is above it by definition, so they stay put).
      const seen = new Uint8Array(WM_N * WM_N);
      for (let k0 = 0; k0 < raw.length; k0++) {
        if (!raw[k0] || lakeMask[k0] || seen[k0]) continue;
        const comp = [k0]; seen[k0] = 1;
        for (let h = 0; h < comp.length; h++) {
          const k = comp[h], i = k % WM_N, j = (k / WM_N) | 0;
          for (const nk of [i > 0 ? k - 1 : -1, i < WM_N - 1 ? k + 1 : -1, j > 0 ? k - WM_N : -1, j < WM_N - 1 ? k + WM_N : -1]) {
            if (nk >= 0 && raw[nk] && !seen[nk] && !lakeMask[nk]) { seen[nk] = 1; comp.push(nk); }
          }
        }
        // Not where a trail runs through the hollow — that is a dip in the path, and
        // flooding it would drown the trail.
        let trail = false;
        try { for (let h = 0; h < comp.length && !trail; h += 2) { const k = comp[h]; if (distToPath(WM_MIN_X + (k % WM_N) * WATER_CELL, WM_MIN_Z + ((k / WM_N) | 0) * WATER_CELL) < 2.5) trail = true; } } catch (_) { trail = true; }
        if (comp.length >= 8 && !trail) for (const k of comp) lakeMask[k] = 1;
      }
    }

    // Is this point inside the solved lake body? Generous by one cell, because the
    // per-point terrain test below is what actually decides the waterline.
    function inLakeBody(x, z) {
      const fi = Math.round((x - WM_MIN_X) / WATER_CELL);
      const fj = Math.round((z - WM_MIN_Z) / WATER_CELL);
      if (fi < 0 || fj < 0 || fi >= WM_N || fj >= WM_N) return false;
      return lakeMask[fj * WM_N + fi] === 1;
    }
    buildWaterMask();

    // Water surface height at a point, or null on dry land.
    // How far out from the river's line its water may reach. The banks decide where it
    // actually stops (the channel climbs out of the water well inside this); this only
    // keeps a dip in a far field from counting as river.
    const RIVER_CORR = RIVER_WIDTH * 1.9;
    function waterLevelAt(x, z) {
      // One water. The lake fills whatever sits below its surface inside the solved
      // body; the river fills its channel up to its own surface at that point along
      // it. Where both reach (the join), they are the same level by construction.
      const g = sampleHeight(x, z);
      let w = null;
      if (inLakeBody(x, z) && g < LAKE.level) w = LAKE.level;
      const p = riverProject(x, z);
      if (p.d < RIVER_CORR) {
        const surf = riverSurfAt(p.s);
        if (g < surf && (w === null || surf > w)) w = surf;
      }
      return w;
    }

    // How deep a point is under water, 0 when dry.
    function waterDepthAt(x, z) {
      const w = waterLevelAt(x, z);
      return w === null ? 0 : Math.max(0, w - sampleHeight(x, z));
    }

    // Everything combat needs to know about the water at a point, in one call:
    //   level    the water surface's height, or null on dry ground
    //   depth    metres of water over the ground (0 when dry)
    //   wading   0 on dry ground, rising to 1 at SWIM_DEPTH, where a body starts to swim
    //   current  { x, z } in m/s: the river's flow here (0, 0 on the lake and on land)
    //   speed    the length of current
    // A bridge or dock over the water isn't taken into account: check the deck first
    // (platformHeightAt) if the body could be standing on one.
    const SWIM_DEPTH = 1.3;
    function waterAt(x, z) {
      const level = waterLevelAt(x, z);
      const depth = level === null ? 0 : Math.max(0, level - sampleHeight(x, z));
      let cx = 0, cz = 0, speed = 0;
      if (depth > 0) {
        speed = waterCurrentAt(x, z);
        if (speed > 0) { const [dx, dz] = riverFlowDir(riverProject(x, z).s); cx = dx * speed; cz = dz * speed; }
      }
      return { level, depth, wading: Math.min(1, depth / SWIM_DEPTH), current: { x: cx, z: cz }, speed };
    }

    // Surface normal from finite differences — used to lay decals/props flat on slopes.
    const AXIS_Z = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 1);
    const AXIS_Y = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0);
    const _nrmA = new THREE.Vector3();
    function terrainNormal(x, z, out) {
      const e = 0.8;
      const hL = sampleHeight(x - e, z), hR = sampleHeight(x + e, z);
      const hD = sampleHeight(x, z - e), hU = sampleHeight(x, z + e);
      return (out || _nrmA).set(hL - hR, 2 * e, hD - hU).normalize();
    }

    // Steepness as 0 (flat) .. 1 (vertical).
    function terrainSlope(x, z) {
      const e = 0.8;
      const hL = sampleHeight(x - e, z), hR = sampleHeight(x + e, z);
      const hD = sampleHeight(x, z - e), hU = sampleHeight(x, z + e);
      const gx = (hR - hL) / (2 * e), gz = (hU - hD) / (2 * e);
      return Math.min(1, Math.hypot(gx, gz) / 2.2);
    }

    // Ground height the marine's boots rest on. Sampling only the centre point left the
    // downhill foot hanging in the air on every slope. Decks (bridges, the dock)
    // override terrain when they're just overhead. The height-difference cap used to
    // be 4.4 — fine for the dock, but a bridge deck is set by the *highest* point
    // along its whole crossing ("so the planks clear the banks and the bed alike"),
    // so anywhere the river channel underneath runs deeper than that near mid-span,
    // the deck lost to the riverbed and the player sank straight through the planks.
    // Being inside a deck's footprint at all is reason enough to stand on the deck.
    function playerGroundY(x, z, maxY) {
      const g = groundMinAround(x, z, 0.3);
      const p = platformHeightAt(x, z, maxY);
      return (p !== null && p > g && p - g < 60) ? p : g;
    }

    // Lowest ground inside a footprint. Props sit on this so nothing floats on a slope.
    function groundMinAround(x, z, r) {
      let m = sampleHeight(x, z);
      if (r > 0.05) {
        for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
          const a = (i / 6) * Math.PI * 2;
          const h = sampleHeight(x + Math.cos(a) * r, z + Math.sin(a) * r);
          if (h < m) m = h;
        }
      }
      return m;
    }

    // landDist / inLand / clampToLand — shared land-bound helpers
    function landDist(x, z) { return Math.hypot(x, z); }
    function inLand(x, z, margin = 0) { return landDist(x, z) <= landRadius - margin; }
    function clampToLand(x, z, margin = 1.5) {
      const maxR = landRadius - margin;
      const d = landDist(x, z);
      if (d <= maxR || d < 1e-8) return { x, z };
      const s = maxR / d;
      return { x: x * s, z: z * s };
    }

    // === Points of interest ===
    // The valley gets inhabited: campsites, ruins, a watchtower, a dock, a graveyard
    // and two river bridges. Locations are solved here (before the ground bakes) so the
    // dirt paths connecting them can be painted into the terrain colours. The meshes
    // themselves are built later, once the prop helpers exist.
    const worldSolids = [];   // { x, z, radius, y0, y1, landmark } — blocks movement, builds, bullets
    const landmarks = [];     // destructible landmarks (cabins, tower, campsites, graveyard, sheds, fences) — shared hp/collapse handling
    const platforms = [];     // { x, z, hw, hl, yaw, deckY } — walkable decks
    const campfires = [];     // { x, z, y, light } — flicker at night
    const POI = { campsites: [], cabins: [], tower: null, graveyard: null, dock: null, bridges: [], sheds: [], wrecks: [], mast: null, fences: [], signs: [], sandbags: null, caves: [] };
    const PATHS = [];         // polylines of {x,z} painted as worn dirt
    const PATH_HUBS = [];     // { x, z, n } — spots where 2+ trails share an endpoint

    // `landmark` tags this collider as belonging to a destructible building (see
    // damageLandmark below) so a bullet or the tower siege can find its way back to an
    // hp pool. Plain scenery (tents, gravestones, bridge posts) passes nothing and stays
    // exactly as indestructible as it always was.
    function addSolid(x, z, radius, y0, y1, landmark = null) {
      const s = { x, z, radius, y0, y1, landmark };
      worldSolids.push(s);
      return s;
    }

    // Deck height at a point, or null when not on any platform.
    // `maxY`, when given, is the highest surface the caller can step onto from where it
    // is: decks above that are overhead and ignored. Without it this returned the FIRST
    // deck under a point with no idea how high you were, which is harmless for a lone
    // bridge but means walking into a building puts you on its roof. With stacked
    // floors there can be several decks over one spot, so this takes the highest one
    // you can actually reach rather than whichever happened to be registered first.
    // Standing on planks (a floor, a platform, the stairs, a bridge or the dock)
    // rather than the ground: boots knock instead of scuff.
    function onBoards() {
      const p = player.position;
      const h = platformHeightAt(p.x, p.z, p.y + 0.3);
      return h != null && Math.abs(h - p.y) < 0.2;
    }
    function platformHeightAt(x, z, maxY) {
      let best = null;
      for (const p of platforms) {
        const dx = x - p.x, dz = z - p.z;
        // World -> deck-local. This has to be the exact inverse of the transform three
        // puts on the deck mesh (rotation.y = yaw, i.e. worldX = lx*cos + lz*sin,
        // worldZ = -lx*sin + lz*cos), which means transposing it:
        //     lx = dx*cos - dz*sin
        //     lz = dx*sin + dz*cos
        // It used to rotate the wrong way, which silently rotated the walkable
        // rectangle to the MIRRORED angle. On any deck not lying near an axis that put
        // the collision footprint nowhere near the planks you can see: standing dead
        // centre on a 45-degree bridge reported ~4m off to the side (so you fell
        // straight through the deck), while thin air out beside it reported as solid
        // (so you hovered). Every "clipping through the bridge", "gap at the bridge",
        // "dock clips through" and "zombies stuck at the bridge" report traces here.
        const c = Math.cos(p.yaw), s = Math.sin(p.yaw);
        const lx = dx * c - dz * s;
        const lz = dx * s + dz * c;
        if (Math.abs(lx) <= p.hw && Math.abs(lz) <= p.hl) {
          // `rise` makes a deck a ramp instead of a shelf: the surface climbs from
          // deckY at the near edge to deckY + rise at the far one. Stairs are just a
          // ramp, which means the player and the horde both walk up them through the
          // ground-height path they already use, rather than needing their own
          // pathing.
          const y = p.rise ? p.deckY + p.rise * (lz / p.hl * 0.5 + 0.5) : p.deckY;
          if (maxY != null && y > maxY) continue;
          if (best === null || y > best) best = y;
        }
      }
      return best;
    }

    // Ground for anything that walks: terrain, unless a deck is just overhead. The
    // ceiling covers a bridge spanning a carved river channel. See playerGroundY for
    // why the cap is generous rather than the old, too-tight 4.4.
    const STEP_UP = 0.75;
    const PLAYER_HEAD = 1.7;

    // The underside of the lowest deck overhead, or null. "Overhead" is a deck whose
    // top is clearly above your feet, so one you are stepping onto never counts, and
    // ramps never do — you walk up those, not under them.
    function deckCeilingAt(x, z, feetY) {
      let best = null;
      for (const p of platforms) {
        if (p.rise) continue;
        if (p.deckY <= feetY + 0.5) continue;
        const dx = x - p.x, dz = z - p.z;
        const c = Math.cos(p.yaw), s = Math.sin(p.yaw);
        const lx = dx * c - dz * s, lz = dx * s + dz * c;
        if (Math.abs(lx) > p.hw || Math.abs(lz) > p.hl) continue;
        const u = p.under != null ? p.under : p.deckY - 0.16;
        if (best === null || u < best) best = u;
      }
      return best;
    }
    // A deck is a solid slab from below. Reject horizontal entry into a space
    // too low for the capsule, rather than allowing terrain to push feet through
    // the underside until the top suddenly qualifies as a step.
    function resolveDeckBody(x, z, feetY, previousX, previousZ, previousY) {
      for (const p of platforms) {
        if (p.rise || previousY >= p.deckY - 0.18) continue;
        const c = Math.cos(p.yaw), sn = Math.sin(p.yaw);
        let lx = (x - p.x) * c - (z - p.z) * sn;
        let lz = (x - p.x) * sn + (z - p.z) * c;
        const hw = p.hw + PLAYER_RADIUS, hl = p.hl + PLAYER_RADIUS;
        if (Math.abs(lx) >= hw || Math.abs(lz) >= hl) continue;
        const oldX = (previousX - p.x) * c - (previousZ - p.z) * sn;
        const oldZ = (previousX - p.x) * sn + (previousZ - p.z) * c;
        const alreadyUnder = Math.abs(oldX) < p.hw && Math.abs(oldZ) < p.hl;
        if (!alreadyUnder && p.deckY <= previousY + STEP_UP) continue; // ordinary entry at the bridge mouth
        const under = p.under != null ? p.under : p.deckY - 0.16;
        const floor = groundMinAround(x, z, 0.3);
        if (Math.max(floor, feetY) + PLAYER_HEAD <= under + 0.01) continue;
        // If ground clearance is sufficient, the vertical ceiling clamp handles a jump.
        if (alreadyUnder && floor + PLAYER_HEAD <= under) continue;
        if (hw - Math.abs(lx) < hl - Math.abs(lz)) lx = (lx < 0 ? -1 : 1) * hw;
        else lz = (lz < 0 ? -1 : 1) * hl;
        x = p.x + lx * c + lz * sn; z = p.z - lx * sn + lz * c;
      }
      return { x, z };
    }
    const playerFrameStart = new THREE.Vector3();

    // How far up (or down) a zombie can reach to hit the player. Under a platform deck,
    // over a single step.
    const ZOMBIE_REACH_Y = 1.45;

    // Is this point on a ramp — a flight of stairs — rather than a shelf or the ground?
    function onRamp(x, z) {
      for (const p of platforms) {
        if (!p.rise) continue;
        const dx = x - p.x, dz = z - p.z;
        const c = Math.cos(p.yaw), s2 = Math.sin(p.yaw);
        if (Math.abs(dx * c - dz * s2) <= p.hw && Math.abs(dx * s2 + dz * c) <= p.hl) return true;
      }
      return false;
    }

    function entityGroundY(x, z, maxY) {
      if (onHqRoof && house.present && Math.abs(x - house.group.position.x) < house.half - 0.2 && Math.abs(z - house.group.position.z) < house.half - 0.2) return hqRoofY();
      const g = sampleHeight(x, z);
      const p = platformHeightAt(x, z, maxY);
      return (p !== null && p > g && p - g < 60) ? p : g;
    }

    // Interpolated point + tangent along the river at arc fraction s.
    function riverPointAt(s) {
      const target = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, s)) * RIVER_LEN;
      for (let i = 0; i < RIVER_CTRL.length - 1; i++) {
        if (RIVER_ARC[i + 1] >= target) {
          const a = RIVER_CTRL[i], b = RIVER_CTRL[i + 1];
          const t = (target - RIVER_ARC[i]) / (RIVER_ARC[i + 1] - RIVER_ARC[i]);
          const len = Math.hypot(b.x - a.x, b.z - a.z) || 1;
          return {
            x: a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t,
            z: a.z + (b.z - a.z) * t,
            tx: (b.x - a.x) / len,
            tz: (b.z - a.z) / len
          };
        }
      }
      const last = RIVER_CTRL[RIVER_CTRL.length - 1];
      return { x: last.x, z: last.z, tx: 1, tz: 0 };
    }

    // Declared up at module scope (rather than down with the tower's other constants)
    // because both planPOIs' path-routing below and buildWatchtower() itself need to
    // agree on exactly where the ladder sits.
    const TOWER_LADDER_OUT = 2.25;  // ladder stands this far out from centre — clear of the base collider (radius 1.75 + player radius 0.42)
    // Bridge deck size, up here because the trail planner walks trails over the decks.
    const BRIDGE_HALF_LEN = 8.2, BRIDGE_HW = 1.35;
    // A footpath's half-width; busier trails are wider (see planPOIs).
    const TRAIL_HW = 0.85;
    // The trampled, packed-earth yard around the HQ that every trail starts from.
    const HQ_YARD_R = 9.5;

    (function planPOIs() {
      const rnd = mulberry32(0x9015eed);
      const taken = [{ x: 0, z: 0, sep: 26 }]; // keep spawn clear

      function findSpot(rMin, rMax, maxSlope, sep) {
        for (let tries = 0; tries < 400; tries++) {
          const a = rnd() * Math.PI * 2;
          const r = rMin + rnd() * (rMax - rMin);
          const x = Math.cos(a) * r, z = Math.sin(a) * r;
          if (waterDepthAt(x, z) > 0.02) continue;
          if (terrainSlope(x, z) > maxSlope) continue;
          if (distToRiver(x, z) < RIVER_WIDTH + 6) continue;
          let ok = true;
          for (const t of taken) {
            if (Math.hypot(x - t.x, z - t.z) < Math.max(sep, t.sep)) { ok = false; break; }
          }
          if (!ok) continue;
          taken.push({ x, z, sep });
          return { x, z };
        }
        return null;
      }

      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        const s = findSpot(40, 115, 0.22, 42);
        if (s) POI.campsites.push(s);
      }
      for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
        const s = findSpot(60, 160, 0.2, 48);
        if (s) POI.cabins.push(s);
      }
      POI.tower = findSpot(90, 170, 0.26, 44);
      POI.graveyard = findSpot(70, 150, 0.18, 44);

      // Dock: walk from the lake centre toward spawn until the ground breaks water.
      {
        const dLen = Math.hypot(LAKE.x, LAKE.z) || 1;
        const dirX = -LAKE.x / dLen, dirZ = -LAKE.z / dLen;
        for (let d = 8; d < LAKE_FILL + 20; d += 1) {
          const x = LAKE.x + dirX * d, z = LAKE.z + dirZ * d;
          if (sampleHeight(x, z) > LAKE.level + 0.15) {
            POI.dock = { x, z, yaw: Math.atan2(-dirX, -dirZ) };
            break;
          }
        }
      }

      // Bridges: two crossings where the river runs inside the play area.
      for (const s of [0.42, 0.66]) {
        const p = riverPointAt(s);
        if (Math.hypot(p.x, p.z) > landRadius - 18) continue;
        POI.bridges.push({
          x: p.x, z: p.z,
          yaw: Math.atan2(-p.tz, p.tx) // deck runs perpendicular to the flow
        });
      }

      // Ruined sheds — smaller than cabins, mid-range scatter.
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        const s = findSpot(45, 130, 0.24, 28);
        if (s) POI.sheds.push(s);
      }

      // Crashed truck wrecks — off roads but findable.
      for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
        const s = findSpot(50, 140, 0.28, 36);
        if (s) POI.wrecks.push(s);
      }

      // Radio mast — skinny lattice silhouette for navigation.
      POI.mast = findSpot(80, 165, 0.22, 40);

      // GP-118 (Jerry): Brandt needs to see the Pit from his deck. The random
      // site stood behind the ridge; this natural shoulder overlooks the lake.
      // Override only after every findSpot roll, preserving the other POI sites.
      // Do this before trail routing so the path still ends at the actual ladder.
      POI.tower = { x: -25, z: -125 };

      // Warning / story props (cheap juice near graveyard, wrecks, one cabin).
      if (POI.graveyard) {
        POI.signs.push({ x: POI.graveyard.x + 4.2, z: POI.graveyard.z - 3.0, kind: 'keepout', yaw: 0.4 });
        POI.signs.push({ x: POI.graveyard.x - 3.6, z: POI.graveyard.z + 3.8, kind: 'hazard', yaw: -0.7 });
      }
      for (const w of POI.wrecks) {
        POI.signs.push({ x: w.x + 3.4, z: w.z + 2.2, kind: 'hazard', yaw: 1.1 });
      }
      if (POI.cabins[0]) POI.sandbags = { x: POI.cabins[0].x, z: POI.cabins[0].z };

      // Trails. These used to be one straight-ish leg from spawn to every landmark,
      // which drew a starburst of thin strips out of the HQ, with two or three legs
      // running side by side for a hundred metres wherever landmarks lay in the same
      // direction. Nobody walks like that. Real trails are a network: a well-worn
      // trunk out of camp that forks, and forks again, with each branch peeling off
      // toward its landmark from wherever it is shortest to leave the main track.
      //
      // So each landmark, nearest first, joins the network at the point that makes the
      // walk cheapest, counting ground already on a trail as cheaper to cover than
      // open grass (TRAIL_EASE). Every leg remembers how many landmarks it serves, and
      // that sets its width: a trunk that carries four destinations is a broad beaten
      // track, a spur out to one wreck is a footpath.
      //
      // A landmark across the river is reached over the nearest bridge: the network
      // runs to the near end of the deck, straight over it, and carries on from the
      // far bank.
      function crossesRiver(ax, az, bx, bz) {
        const n = 14;
        for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) {
          const t = i / n;
          if (distToRiver(ax + (bx - ax) * t, az + (bz - az) * t) < RIVER_WIDTH + 0.5) return true;
        }
        return false;
      }
      // Wading through the lake shallows is not a trail either. The last stretch is
      // exempt so a leg can still end at the dock, right on the waterline.
      function overWater(ax, az, bx, bz) {
        const n = Math.max(4, Math.ceil(Math.hypot(bx - ax, bz - az) / 4));
        for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) {
          const t = i / n;
          if (t > 0.85) break;
          if (waterDepthAt(ax + (bx - ax) * t, az + (bz - az) * t) > 0.05) return true;
        }
        return false;
      }
      // A straight a->b run reads as surveyed rather than worn in. Bow each leg out
      // sideways by a noise-driven amount with its own noise offset (tag), so
      // neighbouring legs don't bulge in lockstep. The bow is exactly 0 at both ends,
      // so a leg still lands on its landmark and leaves the trail it forks from at
      // exactly the junction point.
      let pathTag = 0;
      function wavyLeg(ax, az, bx, bz, straight = false) {
        pathTag += 23.7;
        const tag = pathTag;
        const len = Math.hypot(bx - ax, bz - az);
        const dx = bx - ax, dz = bz - az;
        const nx = len > 1e-4 ? -dz / len : 0, nz = len > 1e-4 ? dx / len : 0;
        const segs = Math.max(2, Math.round(len / 3.5));
        const pts = [{ x: ax, z: az }];
        const maxBow = straight ? 0 : Math.min(5.5, len * 0.2);
        for (let i = 1; i < segs; i++) {
          const t = i / segs;
          const x = ax + dx * t, z = az + dz * t;
          const n = fbm(x * 0.04 + tag, z * 0.04 - tag * 1.7, 2) +
                    fbm(x * 0.011 + tag * 0.31, z * 0.011 - tag * 0.31, 2) * 0.7;
          const taper = smoothstep01(t / 0.16) * smoothstep01((1 - t) / 0.12);
          const amt = n * taper * maxBow;
          pts.push({ x: x + nx * amt, z: z + nz * amt });
        }
        pts.push({ x: bx, z: bz });
        return pts;
      }

      const TRAIL_EASE = 0.55;   // cost of a metre already on a trail vs one of open ground
      const legs = [];           // { pts, cum, parent, at, traffic, deck }
      function cumulative(pts, base) {
        const c = [base];
        for (let i = 1; i < pts.length; i++) c.push(c[i - 1] + Math.hypot(pts[i].x - pts[i - 1].x, pts[i].z - pts[i - 1].z));
        return c;
      }
      // Cut a leg in two at vertex k, so a new branch can hang off the junction and the
      // extra traffic only widens the stretch between it and camp.
      function splitLeg(leg, k) {
        if (k >= leg.pts.length - 1) return leg;
        const tail = { pts: leg.pts.slice(k), cum: leg.cum.slice(k), parent: leg, at: k, traffic: leg.traffic, deck: leg.deck };
        for (const l of legs) {
          if (l.parent === leg && l.at > k) { l.parent = tail; l.at -= k; }
        }
        leg.pts = leg.pts.slice(0, k + 1);
        leg.cum = leg.cum.slice(0, k + 1);
        legs.push(tail);
        return leg;
      }
      const ROOT = { pts: [{ x: 0, z: 0 }], cum: [0], parent: null, traffic: 0 }; // camp itself, as a join result
      function addLeg(parent, pts, deck = false) {
        if (parent === ROOT) parent = null;
        const base = parent ? parent.cum[parent.cum.length - 1] : 0;
        const leg = { pts, cum: cumulative(pts, base), parent, at: parent ? parent.pts.length - 1 : 0, traffic: 1, deck };
        for (let l = parent; l; l = l.parent) l.traffic++;
        legs.push(leg);
        return leg;
      }
      // Join (tx, tz) to the network at the cheapest point that doesn't ford the river
      // or wade the lake. Returns the new leg, or null when nothing qualifies.
      function joinNetwork(tx, tz) {
        let best = null, bestCost = Infinity;
        const consider = (leg, k, x, z, cum) => {
          const d = Math.hypot(tx - x, tz - z);
          const cost = cum * TRAIL_EASE + d;
          if (cost >= bestCost) return;
          if (crossesRiver(x, z, tx, tz) || overWater(x, z, tx, tz)) return;
          best = { leg, k, x, z, d };
          bestCost = cost;
        };
        consider(null, 0, 0, 0, 0);
        for (const leg of legs) {
