          // No forking off halfway across a bridge — only from the bank at its far end.
          for (let k = leg.deck ? leg.pts.length - 1 : 1; k < leg.pts.length; k++) consider(leg, k, leg.pts[k].x, leg.pts[k].z, leg.cum[k]);
        }
        if (!best) return null;
        const parent = best.leg ? splitLeg(best.leg, best.k) : null;
        if (best.d < 3) return parent || ROOT; // already standing on a trail
        return addLeg(parent, wavyLeg(best.x, best.z, tx, tz));
      }
      const bridgeLeg = new Map(); // bridge -> the leg over its deck, once walked
      function crossAt(bridge, tx, tz) {
        let deck = bridgeLeg.get(bridge);
        if (deck) return deck;
        // Deck runs along (sin yaw, cos yaw); step a little past each end onto the bank.
        const reach = BRIDGE_HALF_LEN + 2.5;
        const sx = Math.sin(bridge.yaw), sz = Math.cos(bridge.yaw);
        let ax = bridge.x - sx * reach, az = bridge.z - sz * reach;
        let bx = bridge.x + sx * reach, bz = bridge.z + sz * reach;
        // `b` is the end on the landmark's side.
        if (Math.hypot(ax - tx, az - tz) < Math.hypot(bx - tx, bz - tz)) { [ax, bx] = [bx, ax]; [az, bz] = [bz, az]; }
        const approach = joinNetwork(ax, az);
        if (!approach) return null;
        deck = addLeg(approach, wavyLeg(ax, az, bx, bz, true), true);
        bridgeLeg.set(bridge, deck);
        return deck;
      }
      function addPath(tx, tz) {
        if (joinNetwork(tx, tz)) return;
        // Nothing reaches it on this bank: go by the bridge nearest the landmark.
        let bridge = null, bd = 1e9;
        for (const b of POI.bridges) {
          const d = Math.hypot(b.x - tx, b.z - tz);
          if (d < bd) { bd = d; bridge = b; }
        }
        if (bridge && crossAt(bridge, tx, tz)) joinNetwork(tx, tz);
      }
      const dests = [];
      for (const c of POI.campsites) dests.push(c);
      if (POI.dock) dests.push(POI.dock);
      if (POI.graveyard) dests.push(POI.graveyard);
      // Routed to the ladder's actual foot, not the tower's centre — the tower's own
      // collision cylinder (radius 1.75) sits between the two, so a trail aimed at
      // the centre dead-ends into the wall on whichever side you approach from
      // instead of leading you around to the one spot you can actually climb.
      if (POI.tower) dests.push({ x: POI.tower.x, z: POI.tower.z - TOWER_LADDER_OUT });
      // One worn track each toward the new landmarks (keeps path count reasonable).
      if (POI.sheds[0]) dests.push(POI.sheds[0]);
      if (POI.wrecks[0]) dests.push(POI.wrecks[0]);
      if (POI.mast) dests.push(POI.mast);
      dests.sort((a, b) => Math.hypot(a.x, a.z) - Math.hypot(b.x, b.z));
      for (const d of dests) addPath(d.x, d.z);
      // A bridge nobody's trail happens to cross still gets walked to: a crossing
      // with worn approaches and no path to it looks like it was dropped there.
      for (const b of POI.bridges) {
        if (bridgeLeg.has(b)) continue;
        const reach = BRIDGE_HALF_LEN + 2.5, sx = Math.sin(b.yaw), sz = Math.cos(b.yaw);
        const e1 = { x: b.x - sx * reach, z: b.z - sz * reach }, e2 = { x: b.x + sx * reach, z: b.z + sz * reach };
        const near = Math.hypot(e1.x, e1.z) < Math.hypot(e2.x, e2.z) ? e1 : e2;
        addPath(near.x, near.z);
      }

      // Publish. Width follows traffic: a one-landmark spur is a footpath about 1.7m
      // across, the trunk out of camp a beaten track closer to four. `hw` is the
      // half-width, `bb` a padded bounding box so distance queries can skip whole legs.
      for (const leg of legs) {
        if (leg.pts.length < 2) continue;
        const line = leg.pts;
        line.hw = leg.deck ? BRIDGE_HW : TRAIL_HW + 0.3 * Math.min(4, leg.traffic - 1);
        line.deck = leg.deck;
        let x0 = Infinity, z0 = Infinity, x1 = -Infinity, z1 = -Infinity;
        for (const p of line) { x0 = Math.min(x0, p.x); z0 = Math.min(z0, p.z); x1 = Math.max(x1, p.x); z1 = Math.max(z1, p.z); }
        line.bb = [x0, z0, x1, z1];
        PATHS.push(line);
      }

      // Junctions — where a branch leaves the trail — are trampled a little wider, as
      // people stop, turn and cut the corner. The camp end of every trunk is inside the
      // HQ yard (see yardWearAt), which gets its own treatment.
      (function buildPathHubs() {
        const counts = new Map();
        function bump(p) {
          if (Math.hypot(p.x, p.z) < HQ_YARD_R + 2) return;
          const key = Math.round(p.x * 4) + ',' + Math.round(p.z * 4);
          const e = counts.get(key);
          if (e) e.n++; else counts.set(key, { x: p.x, z: p.z, n: 1 });
        }
        for (const line of PATHS) { if (line.deck) continue; bump(line[0]); bump(line[line.length - 1]); }
        for (const e of counts.values()) if (e.n >= 3) PATH_HUBS.push(e);
      })();

      // Broken fence runs near camps/cabins and along a path corridor.
      {
        const fr = mulberry32(0xf3ace01);
        const anchors = [...POI.campsites, ...POI.cabins];
        for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(3, anchors.length); i++) {
          const a = anchors[i];
          const ang = fr() * Math.PI * 2;
          const len = 9 + fr() * 9;
          const ox = Math.cos(ang) * (5.5 + fr() * 2.5);
          const oz = Math.sin(ang) * (5.5 + fr() * 2.5);
          const dir = ang + 1.15;
          POI.fences.push({
            ax: a.x + ox, az: a.z + oz,
            bx: a.x + ox + Math.cos(dir) * len,
            bz: a.z + oz + Math.sin(dir) * len,
            seed: (fr() * 1e9) | 0
          });
        }
        if (PATHS.length) {
          const line = PATHS[Math.min(1, PATHS.length - 1)];
          const a = line[0], b = line[line.length - 1];
          const dx = b.x - a.x, dz = b.z - a.z;
          const plen = Math.hypot(dx, dz) || 1;
          const nx = -dz / plen, nz = dx / plen;
          const off = 3.2 + fr() * 1.8;
          const t0 = 0.32, t1 = 0.52;
          POI.fences.push({
            ax: a.x + dx * t0 + nx * off, az: a.z + dz * t0 + nz * off,
            bx: a.x + dx * t1 + nx * off, bz: a.z + dz * t1 + nz * off,
            seed: (fr() * 1e9) | 0
          });
        }
      }
    })();

    // --- Approach grading -------------------------------------------------------
    // A bridge or dock deck is one flat height; the ground it lands on is not. The old
    // answer was to park a solid block under the deck end to cover the difference,
    // which read as a floating brown pedestal and — being pure scenery — never matched
    // the height your feet were actually placed at, so you stood buried in it.
    //
    // Instead, reshape the ground: raise (or cut) the cached heightfield into an earth
    // embankment that comes up to meet the deck and eases back into natural terrain
    // over a few metres. The render mesh, the props scattered on it and every height
    // query all read this same field, so what you see, what you walk on and what the
    // deck lands on are one surface — there is nothing left to disagree.
    const DOCK_LEN = 9.5, DOCK_HW = 1.15;

    // Footprints of the ground that got reshaped, so terrainColorAt can paint them as
    // worn earth. An embankment that is still grass-green reads as a strange swelling
    // in the field; as bare dirt it reads as the built-up approach it is.
    const approachPads = [];

    function approachWear(x, z) {
      let out = 0;
      for (const p of approachPads) {
        const dx = x - p.cx, dz = z - p.cz;
        const lx = dx * p.c - dz * p.s;
        const lz = (dx * p.s + dz * p.c) * p.end;
        const al = Math.abs(lx);
        // Ragged edges: the raw lat/along falloff below is a clean rectangle in the
        // pad's own local frame, which reads as a surveyed slab dropped onto the
        // field rather than ground that got walked on. Jitter the effective core and
        // feather/ramp distances with noise keyed to world position (not the pad's
        // local frame, or every pad would fray in lockstep) and fray the result with
        // a second, unrelated noise so the margin thins out in patches.
        const jitter = 1 + fbm(x * 0.22 + p.cx * 0.31, z * 0.22 - p.cz * 0.31, 2) * 0.4;
        if (al > (p.core + p.feather) * 1.5) continue;
        const run = lz - (p.hl - p.inward);
        if (run < 0 || run > (p.inward + p.ramp) * 1.5) continue;
        const core = p.core * jitter, feather = p.feather * jitter, ramp = p.ramp * jitter;
        const lat = al <= core ? 1 : 1 - smoothstep01((al - core) / feather);
        const along = 1 - smoothstep01(Math.max(0, run - p.inward) / ramp);
        // (With the ground detail shader the edge is broken up per pixel there, and
        // fraying the ramp as well only punches grassy holes in the middle of the pad.)
        const fray = GROUND_DETAIL ? 1 : Math.min(1, 0.6 + fbm(x * 0.5 - p.cz * 0.2, z * 0.5 + p.cx * 0.2, 2) * 0.55);
        out = Math.max(out, lat * Math.max(0.3, along) * fray);
      }
      return Math.min(1, out);
    }

    function gradeApproach(cx, cz, yaw, hl, halfWidth, deckY, end, opts = {}) {
      const inward = opts.inward ?? 1.6;    // how far back under the deck to level off
      const ramp = opts.ramp ?? 6;          // graded run reaching out past the deck end
      const feather = opts.feather ?? 3.4;  // lateral blend back into untouched ground
      const lift = opts.lift ?? 0.06;       // sit a hair under the plank surface
      const cutOnly = !!opts.cutOnly;       // dock: lower the bank, never fill the bed
      const core = halfWidth + 0.7;
      const target0 = deckY + lift;
      const c = Math.cos(yaw), s = Math.sin(yaw);
      approachPads.push({ cx, cz, c, s, end, hl, inward, ramp, core, feather });
      const reach = hl + ramp + feather + 3;
      const i0 = Math.max(0, Math.floor((cx - reach + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING));
      const i1 = Math.min(HF_N - 1, Math.ceil((cx + reach + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING));
      const j0 = Math.max(0, Math.floor((cz - reach + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING));
      const j1 = Math.min(HF_N - 1, Math.ceil((cz + reach + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING));
      for (let j = j0; j <= j1; j++) {
        const wz = -HF_EXTENT + j * HF_SPACING;
        for (let i = i0; i <= i1; i++) {
          const wx = -HF_EXTENT + i * HF_SPACING;
          const dx = wx - cx, dz = wz - cz;
          const lx = dx * c - dz * s;
          const lz = (dx * s + dz * c) * end;   // + is toward the end being graded
          const al = Math.abs(lx);
          if (al > core + feather) continue;
          const run = lz - (hl - inward);
          if (run < 0 || run > inward + ramp) continue;
          // 0 while under/at the deck edge, 1 by the tail of the graded run.
          const t = smoothstep01(Math.max(0, run - inward) / ramp);
          const wLat = al <= core ? 1 : 1 - smoothstep01((al - core) / feather);
          const k = j * HF_N + i;
          const natural = heightField[k];
          const target = target0 + (natural - target0) * t;
          if (cutOnly && target > natural) continue;
          heightField[k] = natural + (target - natural) * wLat;
        }
      }
    }

    (function gradeCrossings() {
      // Deck heights first, off untouched ground, so one crossing's embankment can't
      // drag the next one's reading around.
      for (const b of POI.bridges) {
        b.deckY = crestAcrossStrip(b.x, b.z, b.yaw, BRIDGE_HALF_LEN, BRIDGE_HW) + 0.3;
      }
      for (const b of POI.bridges) {
        for (const end of [-1, 1]) {
          // Size the run off the biggest step the approach has to swallow within reach,
          // not just the height right at the deck edge — a bridge often lands on a
          // shoulder that then falls away sharply, and measuring only the edge would
          // give a short, steep ramp diving down a slope that keeps going.
          let drop = 0;
          for (let d = 2; d <= 12; d += 2) {
            const lz = (BRIDGE_HALF_LEN + d) * end;
            const gy = sampleHeight(b.x + Math.sin(b.yaw) * lz, b.z + Math.cos(b.yaw) * lz);
            drop = Math.max(drop, Math.abs(b.deckY - gy));
          }
          const ramp = Math.max(5, Math.min(13, drop * 3.2));
          gradeApproach(b.x, b.z, b.yaw, BRIDGE_HALF_LEN, BRIDGE_HW, b.deckY, end, { ramp });
        }
      }
      if (POI.dock) {
        // The dock's landward half sits over dry ground that keeps climbing inland, so
        // the bank is cut down to meet it. Cut only: the half out over the water must
        // keep its lakebed, or the dock would be standing on a raised shelf.
        POI.dock.deckY = LAKE.level + 0.55;
        gradeApproach(POI.dock.x, POI.dock.z, POI.dock.yaw, DOCK_LEN / 2, DOCK_HW,
          POI.dock.deckY, -1, { inward: DOCK_LEN / 2 + 0.3, ramp: 6.5, lift: 0.04, cutOnly: true });
      }
      // The banks moved, so re-solve which ground the lake still reaches.
      buildWaterMask();
    })();

    // Distance to the nearest trail, measured from a footpath-width trail's edge:
    // a broad trunk reports itself closer by however much wider than a footpath it is.
    // Callers use this for "keep grass tufts / fire / scatter off the track", and
    // those thresholds were tuned for footpaths, so this keeps them honest on the
    // wider stretches too.
    function distToPath(x, z) {
      let best = Infinity;
      for (const line of PATHS) {
        const extra = (line.hw || TRAIL_HW) - TRAIL_HW;
        const bb = line.bb;
        if (bb) {
          const bx = Math.max(bb[0] - x, 0, x - bb[2]), bz = Math.max(bb[1] - z, 0, z - bb[3]);
          if (Math.hypot(bx, bz) - extra >= best) continue;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < line.length - 1; i++) {
          const d = distPointToSeg(x, z, line[i].x, line[i].z, line[i + 1].x, line[i + 1].z) - extra;
          if (d < best) best = d;
        }
      }
      return best;
    }

    // How worn the ground is by foot traffic, as a ramp rather than a finished mask:
    // exactly 0.5 on a trail's edge, climbing to 1 inside it and falling to 0 outside,
    // linearly over TRAIL_FEATHER metres. A linear ramp survives being sampled at the
    // terrain's vertices and interpolated across its triangles intact, so the ground
    // shader can threshold it at 0.5 (with noise) and cut a crisp, ragged trail edge
    // far finer than the mesh itself — which is what turns the old soft, blurred
    // stripes into trails with real edges.
    const TRAIL_FEATHER = 1.3;
    function pathWearAt(x, z) {
      let best = 0;
      const wob = 1 + fbm(x * 0.07 + 5.1, z * 0.07 - 9.3, 2) * 0.28;
      for (const line of PATHS) {
        if (line.deck) continue;
        const hw = (line.hw || TRAIL_HW) * wob;
        const reach = hw + TRAIL_FEATHER;
        const bb = line.bb;
        if (bb && (x < bb[0] - reach || x > bb[2] + reach || z < bb[1] - reach || z > bb[3] + reach)) continue;
        for (let i = 0; i < line.length - 1; i++) {
          const d = distPointToSeg(x, z, line[i].x, line[i].z, line[i + 1].x, line[i + 1].z);
          if (d >= reach) continue;
          const w = 0.5 + 0.5 * (hw - d) / TRAIL_FEATHER;
          if (w > best) best = w;
        }
      }
      return Math.min(1, best);
    }

    // The HQ's yard: the ground around the building is packed earth and grit, beaten
    // flat by everyone coming and going — it is where every trail starts. A rounded
    // square (the building is square) with a noisy rim, on the same 0.5-at-the-edge
    // ramp as the trails.
    function yardWearAt(x, z) {
      const ax = Math.abs(x), az = Math.abs(z);
      if (ax > HQ_YARD_R + 6 || az > HQ_YARD_R + 6) return 0;
      const d = Math.pow(ax ** 3 + az ** 3, 1 / 3);
      const r = HQ_YARD_R * (1 + fbm(x * 0.07 + 3.1, z * 0.07 - 7.7, 2) * 0.32 + fbm(x * 0.25 - 1.3, z * 0.25 + 4.4, 2) * 0.08);
      return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, 0.5 + 0.5 * (r - d) / 2.4));
    }

    // Where a branch leaves a trail the ground is trampled a little wider — people
    // stop, turn, cut the corner. Same ramp again.
    function hubClearingAt(x, z) {
      let best = 0;
      for (const hub of PATH_HUBS) {
        const d = Math.hypot(x - hub.x, z - hub.z);
        const radius = (1.9 + Math.min(3, hub.n - 2) * 0.45) * (1 + fbm(x * 0.12 + hub.x, z * 0.12 - hub.z, 2) * 0.3);
        const t = 0.5 + 0.5 * (radius - d) / 1.6;
        if (t > best) best = t;
      }
      return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, best));
    }

    // Clearance test so scattered props stay out of the landmarks' yards.
    function nearPOI(x, z, clearance = 9) {
      for (const c of POI.campsites) if (Math.hypot(x - c.x, z - c.z) < clearance) return true;
      for (const c of POI.cabins) if (Math.hypot(x - c.x, z - c.z) < clearance) return true;
      if (POI.tower && Math.hypot(x - POI.tower.x, z - POI.tower.z) < clearance) return true;
      if (POI.graveyard && Math.hypot(x - POI.graveyard.x, z - POI.graveyard.z) < clearance + 2) return true;
      if (POI.dock && Math.hypot(x - POI.dock.x, z - POI.dock.z) < clearance + 3) return true;
      for (const b of POI.bridges) if (Math.hypot(x - b.x, z - b.z) < clearance + 3) return true;
      for (const s of POI.sheds) if (Math.hypot(x - s.x, z - s.z) < clearance) return true;
      for (const w of POI.wrecks) if (Math.hypot(x - w.x, z - w.z) < clearance + 1) return true;
      if (POI.mast && Math.hypot(x - POI.mast.x, z - POI.mast.z) < clearance) return true;
      for (const c of POI.caves) if (Math.hypot(x - c.x, z - c.z) < clearance + 3) return true;
      return false;
    }

    // === Ground mesh ===
    // A tessellated radial grid covering the whole world, built once. Every vertex is
    // placed with sampleHeight(), so what you see is exactly what gameplay collides
    // against. (The old mesh was a CircleGeometry — a 192-triangle fan spanning the
    // entire map from a single centre vertex — so the rendered surface bore almost no
    // relation to sampleHeight() and everything sank into or floated above it.)
    // Expanding land only re-tints vertex colours; the surface never changes.
    const TERRAIN_RINGS = 260;
    const TERRAIN_SEGS = 512;
    const TERRAIN_RING_POW = 1.55; // packs rings tighter near the middle of the map
    const TERRAIN_VERTS = 1 + TERRAIN_RINGS * TERRAIN_SEGS;

    const groundBaseColors = new Float32Array(TERRAIN_VERTS * 3);
    const groundVertRadius = new Float32Array(TERRAIN_VERTS);
    // The bare-earth colour and wear ramp per vertex, for the ground shader's trails
    // (see buildGroundDetailMaterial). Kept alongside groundBaseColors and put through
    // the same contact shading and land tint, so a trail darkens under a tree and
    // greys out past the purchased land exactly as the grass beside it does.
    const groundWornColors = new Float32Array(TERRAIN_VERTS * 3);
    const groundWear = new Float32Array(TERRAIN_VERTS);
    // Copy terrainColorAt's outputs (base in _terrCol, worn in _terrWorn/_terrWear)
    // into the per-vertex stores.
    function storeTerrainVertex(vi) {
      const i3 = vi * 3;
      groundBaseColors[i3] = _terrCol.r;
      groundBaseColors[i3 + 1] = _terrCol.g;
      groundBaseColors[i3 + 2] = _terrCol.b;
      groundWornColors[i3] = _terrWorn.r;
      groundWornColors[i3 + 1] = _terrWorn.g;
      groundWornColors[i3 + 2] = _terrWorn.b;
      groundWear[vi] = _terrWear;
    }

    // Biome palette. Ground colour is chosen by altitude, steepness and moisture rather
    // than a single noise band, so the map reads as places instead of texture.
    //
    // This is an alpine valley in late summer: a river out of the eastern peaks and a
    // cold lake in the south-west. The greens lean warm and olive rather than mint
    // (the old palette's blue-leaning green read as a lawn, or a golf course); they
    // run rich and deep where the ground is wet and fade to straw on the exposed
    // rises. Above the valley floor the turf thins to heath before the rock, and the
    // lake's shore is grey-brown shingle, as mountain lakes have, not a tropical beach.
    const cGrassLush = new THREE.Color(0x4b8a42);
    const cGrassMid = new THREE.Color(0x66984c);
    const cGrassDry = new THREE.Color(0x98965c);
    const cMeadow = new THREE.Color(0x7aa151);
    const cGrassDeep = new THREE.Color(0x417a40);
    const cHeath = new THREE.Color(0x857d4c);   // thin alpine turf, bilberry and dry moss
    const cDirt = new THREE.Color(0x7a6649);
    const cDirtWorn = new THREE.Color(0x5c4b38); // packed, shadowed centre of a heavily-trodden track
    const cDirtPale = new THREE.Color(0x9c8a6a); // dusty, sun-bleached where it dries out
    const cMud = new THREE.Color(0x4c3d2c);      // trails soften to mud near water
    const cGravel = new THREE.Color(0x8b8373);   // the HQ yard: packed earth and grit
    const cRock = new THREE.Color(0x807b72);
    const cRockDark = new THREE.Color(0x585a5c);
    const cScree = new THREE.Color(0x8e8a82);
    const cSnow = new THREE.Color(0xeef3f7);
    const cSand = new THREE.Color(0xb2a583);     // lake shingle
    const cSilt = new THREE.Color(0x6d6448);
    // Beds under the water: pale sand in the shallows, olive silt going deeper, dark
    // ooze in the deeps, green where weed has taken the bottom, grey cobble in the
    // river's run.
    const cBedSand = new THREE.Color(0xa39271);
    const cBedSilt = new THREE.Color(0x5f5c40);
    const cBedDeep = new THREE.Color(0x2c3226);
    const cBedWeed = new THREE.Color(0x35532a);
    const cBedCobble = new THREE.Color(0x7c7a71);
    const cDamp = new THREE.Color(0x4a4a2e);
    const cLocked = new THREE.Color(0x24382c);
    const _terrCol = new THREE.Color();
    const _terrCol2 = new THREE.Color();
    const _terrCol3 = new THREE.Color();
    // Second output of terrainColorAt: the colour this spot takes where it is worn to
    // bare earth, and how worn it is (the 0.5-at-the-edge ramp — see pathWearAt).
    const _terrWorn = new THREE.Color();
    let _terrWear = 0;
    // Set once the ground's detail material is built. With it, the ground shader cuts
    // the trails itself from the worn colour and the wear ramp; without it (the plain
    // fallback material) the trails are baked straight into the vertex colour.
    let GROUND_DETAIL = false;

    function terrainColorAt(wx, wz, h, out) {
      const slope = terrainSlope(wx, wz);
      const r = Math.hypot(wx, wz);

      // Moisture: high near water, low on exposed high ground, plus large-scale drift
      // so meadows and dry patches form regions rather than speckle.
      const riverD = distToRiver(wx, wz);
      const lakeD = lakeDist(wx, wz);
      let moisture = 0.5 + fbm(wx * 0.0065 + 21.7, wz * 0.0065 - 13.2, 3) * 0.42;
      moisture += 0.45 * smoothstep01(1 - riverD / 26);
      moisture += 0.40 * smoothstep01(1 - lakeD / (LAKE.r + 30));
      moisture -= smoothBand(6, 30, h) * 0.45;
      // Crests dry out, hollows hold water.
      const e = 3.4;
      const avg = (sampleHeight(wx - e, wz) + sampleHeight(wx + e, wz) +
                   sampleHeight(wx, wz - e) + sampleHeight(wx, wz + e)) * 0.25;
      moisture -= Math.max(-0.12, Math.min(0.15, (h - avg) * 0.08));
      moisture = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, moisture));

      // Grass base, drier as moisture drops.
      out.copy(cGrassDry).lerp(cGrassMid, smoothstep01(moisture * 1.6));
      if (moisture > 0.6) out.lerp(cGrassLush, smoothstep01((moisture - 0.6) / 0.4));

      // Two scales of patchiness. Without this, flat open ground reads as one solid
      // sheet of green no matter how good the landform underneath is.
      const patchBig = fbm(wx * 0.011 + 61.3, wz * 0.011 - 44.1, 2);
      out.lerp(cMeadow, Math.max(0, patchBig) * 0.4);
      out.lerp(cGrassDeep, Math.max(0, -patchBig) * 0.3);
      const patch = fbm(wx * 0.045, wz * 0.045, 2);
      out.lerp(cGrassDry, Math.max(0, patch) * 0.2 * (1 - moisture * 0.6));
      out.multiplyScalar(1 + patch * 0.06);

      // Up out of the valley the turf thins to heath before it gives way to rock.
      const heath = smoothBand(14, 34, h + fbm(wx * 0.02 + 8.8, wz * 0.02 - 2.2, 2) * 8);
      if (heath > 0) out.lerp(cHeath, heath * 0.75);

      // Slope: soil shows through on inclines, bare rock on anything steep.
      // Cave hills have stood long enough to grass over: turf holds on slopes that
      // would be bare anywhere else, and where rock does show it is the cave's own.
      const caveHill = POI.caves.length ? caveHillAt(wx, wz) : 0;
      const turf = caveHill * (caveHill > 0 ? (_caveHillDesign.turf ?? 0.6) : 0);
      out.lerp(cDirt, smoothBand(0.26, 0.48, slope) * 0.75 * (1 - turf * 0.85));
      const rocky = Math.max(smoothBand(0.40, 0.66, slope) * (1 - turf) + (caveHill > 0 ? smoothBand(0.6, 0.95, slope) * caveHill * (1 - turf) * 0.5 : 0),
        caveHill > 0 ? _caveCutRock * smoothBand(0.3, 0.6, slope) : 0);
      if (rocky > 0) {
        const grain = fbm(wx * 0.09, wz * 0.09, 2);
        // Faint strata: rock faces weather in horizontal bands.
        const strata = Math.sin(h * 0.9 + fbm(wx * 0.03, wz * 0.03, 2) * 3) * 0.5 + 0.5;
        _terrCol2.copy(cRock).lerp(cRockDark, 0.35 + grain * 0.45 + strata * 0.2);
        if (caveHill > 0) _terrCol3.set(_caveHillDesign.rock), _terrCol2.lerp(_terrCol3.multiplyScalar(0.85 + strata * 0.3), caveHill * 0.75);
        out.lerp(_terrCol2, Math.min(1, rocky));
      }

      // High ground turns to scree then snow.
      const alt = smoothBand(34, 62, h);
      if (alt > 0) out.lerp(cScree, alt * 0.8);
      const snow = smoothBand(58, 84, h + fbm(wx * 0.012, wz * 0.012, 2) * 9);
      // Snow only settles where it is not near-vertical.
      if (snow > 0) out.lerp(cSnow, snow * (1 - smoothBand(0.55, 0.8, slope)));

      // Shorelines: shingle at the lake, silt along the river. The beach holds full
      // strength right across the shore and is keyed only to height above the
      // waterline, giving the eye a band to cross between grass and water.
      const shoreT = smoothstep01((LAKE_REACH - 8 - lakeD) / 25);
      // The height window is kept fairly tight on purpose: widening it barely changes
      // a normal beach (about 4m either way) but on the flat stretches of shore it runs
      // away, turning 30m of ground into desert.
      // ...and only in stretches. A beach ringing the whole lake reads as a sand
      // outline drawn round a puddle; real shores go from shingle to mud to grass
      // right down to the water and back.
      const beachPatch = 0.2 + 0.8 * smoothstep01((fbm(wx * 0.03 + 9.1, wz * 0.03 - 4.4, 2) + 0.05) / 0.35);
      const beach = smoothstep01(1 - Math.abs(h - LAKE.level - 0.25) / 1.4) * shoreT * beachPatch;
      // A river's silt margin measured as pure distance-from-centreline comes out a
      // dead-straight, constant-width ribbon wherever the bank itself runs straight.
      // Wobbling the effective width with noise gives the bank a ragged edge.
      const riverWobble = 1 + fbm(wx * 0.09 + 77.2, wz * 0.09 - 19.6, 2) * 0.35;
      const siltBand = smoothstep01(1 - riverD / ((RIVER_WIDTH + 2.2) * riverWobble)) * 0.85 * (0.35 + 0.65 * smoothstep01((fbm(wx * 0.05 - 3.3, wz * 0.05 + 8.8, 2) + 0.1) / 0.3));
      if (beach > siltBand) out.lerp(cSand, beach);
      else if (siltBand > 0) out.lerp(cSilt, siltBand * 0.8);

      // --- Wear: trails, the HQ yard, junctions, bridge and dock approaches ---------
      // All on one 0..1 ramp (0.5 = the edge). The bare-earth colour is mottled with
      // a darker packed tone and a paler dusty one, turns to mud toward the water, and
      // to grit in the yard, where boots and pallets and vehicles have packed it hard.
      const yard = yardWearAt(wx, wz);
      // The graded bridge and dock approaches: their footprint ramp is a broad soft
      // pad, so only its stronger core is taken as bare ground once the shader is
      // cutting edges — otherwise the whole embankment flares into a dirt apron much
      // wider than the deck it leads onto.
      const ap = approachWear(wx, wz);
      const apWear = GROUND_DETAIL ? Math.max(0, Math.min(1, 0.5 + (ap - 0.8) * 2.0)) : ap;
      // Cave dooryards (only once the caves are planned).
      const caveW = POI.caves.length ? caveApronWear(wx, wz) : 0;
      const wear = Math.max(pathWearAt(wx, wz), yard, hubClearingAt(wx, wz), apWear, caveW);
      _terrWear = wear;
      if (wear > 0) {
        const tone = fbm(wx * 0.2 - 5.8, wz * 0.2 + 12.4, 2);
        _terrWorn.copy(cDirt);
        if (tone > 0.1) _terrWorn.lerp(cDirtPale, Math.min(1, (tone - 0.1) * 1.3));
        else if (tone < -0.1) _terrWorn.lerp(cDirtWorn, Math.min(1, (-tone - 0.1) * 1.3));
        _terrWorn.lerp(cMud, smoothBand(0.62, 0.95, moisture) * 0.65);
        if (yard > 0) _terrWorn.lerp(cGravel, smoothBand(0.5, 0.95, yard) * 0.45);
        // Shingle and silt stay what they are where a trail meets the shore.
        if (beach > 0.2) _terrWorn.lerp(cSand, beach * 0.6);
        if (caveW > 0.3 && _caveApronTone) _terrWorn.lerp(_caveApronTone, smoothBand(0.3, 0.9, caveW) * 0.6);
      } else {
        _terrWorn.copy(cDirt);
      }

      // Underwater beds, which the water now lets you see: sand in the shallows, silt
      // and ooze with depth, weed beds in patches, cobble down the river's run.
      const wlv = waterLevelAt(wx, wz);
      const depth = wlv === null ? 0 : Math.max(0, wlv - h);
      if (depth > 0) {
        const nw = fbm(wx * 0.07 + 3.1, wz * 0.07 - 7.7, 2), ns = fbm(wx * 0.33 - 1.3, wz * 0.33 + 4.4, 2);
        _terrCol2.copy(cBedSand).lerp(cBedSilt, smoothstep01((depth - 0.15) / 0.8));
        _terrCol2.lerp(cBedDeep, smoothstep01((depth - 1.3) / 2.6));
        const weedy = smoothstep01((nw - 0.02) / 0.22) * smoothstep01((depth - 0.35) / 0.4) * (1 - smoothstep01((depth - 3) / 2));
        _terrCol2.lerp(cBedWeed, weedy * 0.75);
        const run = waterCurrentAt(wx, wz);
        if (run > 0.05) _terrCol2.lerp(cBedCobble, smoothstep01(run / 0.8) * (0.45 + 0.35 * ns));
        _terrCol2.multiplyScalar(1 + ns * 0.12);
        const k = smoothstep01(depth / 0.25);
        out.lerp(_terrCol2, k);
        _terrWorn.lerp(_terrCol2, k);
      } else {
        // A damp margin just above the waterline, darker where the water has been.
        const pot = waterPotentialLevel(wx, wz);
        if (pot !== null) {
          const above = h - pot;
          if (above >= 0 && above < 0.45) {
            const damp = (1 - above / 0.45) * 0.55;
            out.lerp(cDamp, damp * 0.5).multiplyScalar(1 - damp * 0.25);
            _terrWorn.lerp(cDamp, damp * 0.5).multiplyScalar(1 - damp * 0.25);
          }
        }
      }

      // Cheap cavity shading: compare against the local average so gullies darken and
      // ridge crests catch light. Gives the mesh depth without a single extra light.
      // Weighted so crests brighten more than hollows darken — symmetric shading here
      // just drains light out of the whole valley floor.
      const cavity = Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, (h - avg) * 0.42));
      const ck = 1 + cavity * (cavity > 0 ? 0.24 : 0.11);
      out.multiplyScalar(ck);
      _terrWorn.multiplyScalar(ck);

      // Distant peaks drift toward the sky so the far ridgeline sits back in the haze.
      const far = smoothBand(250, TERRAIN_RADIUS, r);
      if (far > 0) { out.lerp(cSnow, far * 0.10); _terrWorn.lerp(cSnow, far * 0.10); }

      // Without the detail shader to cut the trail edge, bake a soft version in.
      if (!GROUND_DETAIL && wear > 0) out.lerp(_terrWorn, smoothBand(0.3, 0.75, wear) * 0.85);

      return out;
    }

    function buildGroundGeometry() {
      const rings = TERRAIN_RINGS, segs = TERRAIN_SEGS;
      const positions = new Float32Array(TERRAIN_VERTS * 3);
      const colors = new Float32Array(TERRAIN_VERTS * 3);

      const h0 = sampleHeight(0, 0);
      positions[1] = h0;
      terrainColorAt(0, 0, h0, _terrCol);
      storeTerrainVertex(0);

      for (let i = 1; i <= rings; i++) {
        const r = TERRAIN_RADIUS * Math.pow(i / rings, TERRAIN_RING_POW);
        for (let j = 0; j < segs; j++) {
          const a = (j / segs) * Math.PI * 2;
          const x = Math.cos(a) * r, z = Math.sin(a) * r;
          const h = sampleHeight(x, z);
          const vi = 1 + (i - 1) * segs + j;
          positions[vi * 3] = x;
          positions[vi * 3 + 1] = h;
          positions[vi * 3 + 2] = z;
          terrainColorAt(x, z, h, _terrCol);
          storeTerrainVertex(vi);
          groundVertRadius[vi] = r;
        }
      }

      const indices = new Uint32Array((segs + (rings - 1) * segs * 2) * 3);
      let k = 0;
      for (let j = 0; j < segs; j++) {
        indices[k++] = 0;
        indices[k++] = 1 + ((j + 1) % segs);
        indices[k++] = 1 + j;
      }
      for (let i = 1; i < rings; i++) {
        const inner = 1 + (i - 1) * segs;
        const outer = 1 + i * segs;
        for (let j = 0; j < segs; j++) {
          const j2 = (j + 1) % segs;
          const a = inner + j, b = inner + j2, c = outer + j2, d = outer + j;
          indices[k++] = a; indices[k++] = b; indices[k++] = c;
          indices[k++] = a; indices[k++] = c; indices[k++] = d;
        }
      }

      const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
      geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3));
      geo.setAttribute('color', new THREE.BufferAttribute(colors, 3));
      geo.setAttribute('gworn', new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(TERRAIN_VERTS * 3), 3));
      geo.setAttribute('gwear', new THREE.BufferAttribute(groundWear, 1));
      geo.setIndex(new THREE.BufferAttribute(indices, 1));
      geo.computeVertexNormals();
      geo.computeBoundingSphere();
      return geo;
    }

    // === Ground detail ===========================================================
    // Vertex colour alone tops out at the mesh's resolution — a metre or more between
    // vertices out in the field — so on its own the ground is smooth, airbrushed
    // colour: grass with no grain to it, and trails that are soft blurred stripes
    // because a trail edge can be no sharper than the triangles it is painted across.
    //
    // The detail material fixes both in the shader. One small tiling texture, sampled
    // in world space at three scales, gives the grass clumps and grain (and grit and
    // pebbles on anything bare), and slow, map-sized colour drift so no two meadows
    // are the same green. The trails are no longer painted into the vertex colour at
    // all: each vertex carries the bare-earth colour for that spot and a wear ramp
    // that crosses 0.5 exactly on the trail's edge, and the shader cuts the trail
    // where the ramp, jittered by the texture, crosses that line — a crisp, ragged
    // edge at pixel resolution, however coarse the mesh underneath. Grass along the
    // margin is trampled paler before it gives out.
    //
    // ?ground=flat forces the plain vertex-colour material (trails baked in, softly),
    // and any failure building the node material falls back to it too.
    const GROUND_FORCE_FLAT = /[?&]ground=flat(&|=|$)/i.test(location.search);

    // Tileable value noise on a size x size grid, `cells` lattice cells across.
    function tileNoise(size, cells, rnd) {
      const lat = new Float32Array(cells * cells);
      for (let i = 0; i < lat.length; i++) lat[i] = rnd();
      const out = new Float32Array(size * size);
      for (let y = 0; y < size; y++) {
        const fy = y / size * cells, y0 = Math.floor(fy), ty = fy - y0;
        const sy = ty * ty * (3 - 2 * ty);
        const r0 = (y0 % cells) * cells, r1 = ((y0 + 1) % cells) * cells;
        for (let x = 0; x < size; x++) {
          const fx = x / size * cells, x0 = Math.floor(fx), tx = fx - x0;
          const sx = tx * tx * (3 - 2 * tx);
          const c0 = x0 % cells, c1 = (x0 + 1) % cells;
          const a = lat[r0 + c0] + (lat[r0 + c1] - lat[r0 + c0]) * sx;
          const b = lat[r1 + c0] + (lat[r1 + c1] - lat[r1 + c0]) * sx;
          out[y * size + x] = a + (b - a) * sy;
        }
      }
      return out;
    }
    // Three data channels, not a picture: R = grass clumping and grain, G = grit with
    // scattered pebbles, B = soft blotches (trail-edge breakup and colour drift).
    // Every value averages about 0.5, so the shader can use them as +/- offsets.
    function makeGroundDetailTexture() {
      const N = 256;

      const j0 = Math.max(0, Math.floor((z0 - F + HF_EXTENT) / HF_SPACING));

      const pos = geo.getAttribute('position');

    // === Contact shading =========================================================

      // just drain the colour from the mountain backdrop.

      for (let i = 0; i < TERRAIN_VERTS; i++) {

    updateLandTint();

    // === Water ===

    const WAVE_K = { xFreq: 0.42, xTime: 2.1, zFreq: 0.31, zTime: 1.5, zAmp: 0.8 };

      const { uniform, vec3, vec4, sin, attribute } = TSL;
      if (!waterTimeUniform) waterTimeUniform = uniform(0);
      const t = waterTimeUniform;
      const P = TSL.positionLocal;
      const wave = sin(P.x.mul(WAVE_K.xFreq).add(t.mul(freq * WAVE_K.xTime))).mul(amp)
        .add(sin(P.z.mul(WAVE_K.zFreq).sub(t.mul(freq * WAVE_K.zTime))).mul(amp * WAVE_K.zAmp));
      const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardNodeMaterial(WATER_SURFACE);
      mat.positionNode = vec3(P.x, P.y.add(wave), P.z);
      // MeshStandardNodeMaterial does not honour vertex-colour alpha on its own —
      // without this the river mouthFade / bank feather was ignored on the GPU path
      // and the ribbon ended on a hard rectangular cut over the lake.
      const vc = attribute('color', 'vec4');
      mat.colorNode = vc.xyz;
      mat.opacityNode = vc.w.mul(WATER_SURFACE.opacity);
      return mat;
    }

    // Called once per wave surface, right after it is registered. On success the mesh
    // gets its own node material and drops out of the CPU loop; on failure it keeps the
    // shared material and the CPU loop keeps waving it, exactly as before.
    function tryGpuWater(w) {
      if (WATER_FORCE_CPU) return false;
      try {
        w.mesh.material = buildWaterMaterial(w.amp, w.freq);
        w.gpu = true;
        waterOnGPU = true;
        return true;
      } catch (err) {
        console.warn('Grave Shift: GPU water failed to build, keeping the CPU wave.', err);
        w.gpu = false;
        return false;
      }
    }

    function buildRiverStations(step = 3) {
      const pts = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < RIVER_CTRL.length - 1; i++) {
        const a = RIVER_CTRL[i], b = RIVER_CTRL[i + 1];
        const n = Math.max(1, Math.round(Math.hypot(b.x - a.x, b.z - a.z) / step));
        for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
          const t = k / n;
          pts.push({ x: a.x + (b.x - a.x) * t, z: a.z + (b.z - a.z) * t });
        }
      }
      const last = RIVER_CTRL[RIVER_CTRL.length - 1];
      pts.push({ x: last.x, z: last.z });
      for (const p of pts) {
        p.r = Math.hypot(p.x, p.z);
        // Surface rides the solved bed, so the river runs downhill the whole way.
        p.y = riverBedAt(riverProject(p.x, p.z).s) + 1.05;
      }
      // Averaged tangents give a mitred ribbon with no overlap at the bends.
      for (let i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) {
        const a = pts[Math.max(0, i - 1)], b = pts[Math.min(pts.length - 1, i + 1)];
        const tx = b.x - a.x, tz = b.z - a.z;
        const len = Math.hypot(tx, tz) || 1;
        pts[i].nx = -tz / len;
        pts[i].nz = tx / len;
      }
      return pts;
    }

    // === The water surface ========================================================
    // One sheet for all of it — lake and river together — laid on a regular grid over
    // every patch of ground that sits below its water, and a cell beyond so the sheet
    // always runs on under the bank. The terrain standing above the surface is what
    // draws the waterline, so it follows every bay, spit and bend exactly.
    //
    // It replaces a river ribbon and a separate lake sheet that met at the river's
    // mouth. They were two surfaces at two heights over one join, and every attempt
    // to hide the seam (fading one, notching the other) left either a box or a dry
    // gap. Here there is no join: the river's surface comes down to the lake's level
    // (see solveRiverBed) and one mesh carries both.
    //
    // Each vertex carries what the shader needs to draw water rather than paint:
    //   wdepth  metres of water over the bed (negative under the bank)
    //   wflow   downstream direction (x, z), current speed (m/s), and how much of it
    //           is open lake (1) rather than running river (0)
    // The shader turns those into colour (clear and pale over the shallows, blue with
    // depth), an alpha that lets the bed, the weed and the fish show through, a
    // surface pattern that is carried downstream on the river and drifts on the lake,
    // a slight swell on the open lake, and foam where the water laps the shore or runs
    // fast over the shallows.
    const WATER_CELL_M = 1.25;
    const waterSurfaceTargets = [];
    const WATER_TINT = {
      shallow: [0.30, 0.52, 0.47], mid: [0.10, 0.36, 0.50], deep: [0.035, 0.18, 0.32],
      sky: [0.60, 0.74, 0.84], foam: [0.88, 0.93, 0.92]
    };
    // A small tileable noise texture, three independent octave stacks in R, G and B.
    const waterNoiseTex = (() => {
      const N = 128, cv = document.createElement('canvas');
      cv.width = cv.height = N;
      const ctx = cv.getContext('2d'), img = ctx.createImageData(N, N);
      const lattice = (P, seed) => { const g = new Float32Array(P * P); const r = mulberry32(seed); for (let i = 0; i < g.length; i++) g[i] = r(); return g; };
      const chan = (seed) => {
        const out = new Float32Array(N * N);

        for (const P of [4, 8, 16, 32]) {
          const g = lattice(P, seed + P * 131);
          for (let y = 0; y < N; y++) for (let x = 0; x < N; x++) {
            const fx = x / N * P, fy = y / N * P, ix = Math.floor(fx), iy = Math.floor(fy);
            let tx = fx - ix, ty = fy - iy; tx = tx * tx * (3 - 2 * tx); ty = ty * ty * (3 - 2 * ty);
            const a = g[(iy % P) * P + (ix % P)], b = g[(iy % P) * P + ((ix + 1) % P)];
            const c = g[((iy + 1) % P) * P + (ix % P)], d = g[((iy + 1) % P) * P + ((ix + 1) % P)];
            out[y * N + x] += ((a + (b - a) * tx) + ((c + (d - c) * tx) - (a + (b - a) * tx)) * ty) * amp;
          }
          tot += amp; amp *= 0.55;
        }
        for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i++) out[i] /= tot;
        // Stretch to the full range so the pattern has contrast to work with.
        let lo = 1, hi = 0; for (const v of out) { if (v < lo) lo = v; if (v > hi) hi = v; }
        for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i++) out[i] = (out[i] - lo) / (hi - lo || 1);
        return out;
      };
      const R = chan(0x51ea), G = chan(0x7a11), B = chan(0x3c0d);
      for (let i = 0; i < N * N; i++) {
        img.data[i * 4] = R[i] * 255; img.data[i * 4 + 1] = G[i] * 255; img.data[i * 4 + 2] = B[i] * 255; img.data[i * 4 + 3] = 255;
      }
      ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
      const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(cv);
      tex.wrapS = tex.wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping;
      tex.colorSpace = THREE.NoColorSpace;
      tex.generateMipmaps = true;
      return tex;
    })();

    // The river's downstream direction at s, smoothed over a few metres so the current
    // turns through a bend instead of snapping at each control point.
    function riverFlowDir(s) {
      const a = riverPointAt(Math.max(0, s - 0.012)), b = riverPointAt(Math.min(1, s + 0.012));
      let dx = b.x - a.x, dz = b.z - a.z; const l = Math.hypot(dx, dz) || 1;
      return [dx / l, dz / l];
    }
    // Current speed along the river: brisk through the channel, quicker down the run
    // into the lake, and gone once it is lake.
    function riverSpeedAt(s) {
      const base = 0.85 + 0.35 * Math.sin(s * 23.0 + 1.3) * 0.5;
      const run = smoothstep01((s - (RIVER_JOIN_S - 0.07)) / 0.05) * (1 - smoothstep01((s - RIVER_JOIN_S) / 0.02));
      const stilled = 1 - smoothstep01((s - RIVER_JOIN_S) / 0.05);
      return (base + run * 0.6) * stilled;
    }

    function buildWaterSurface() {
      const C = WATER_CELL_M;
      // The area worth looking at: the lake's reach, and the river's corridor.
      let minX = LAKE.x - LAKE_REACH, maxX = LAKE.x + LAKE_REACH, minZ = LAKE.z - LAKE_REACH, maxZ = LAKE.z + LAKE_REACH;
      for (const c of RIVER_CTRL) { minX = Math.min(minX, c.x - 14); maxX = Math.max(maxX, c.x + 14); minZ = Math.min(minZ, c.z - 14); maxZ = Math.max(maxZ, c.z + 14); }
      minX = Math.max(minX, -HF_EXTENT + 1); minZ = Math.max(minZ, -HF_EXTENT + 1);
      maxX = Math.min(maxX, HF_EXTENT - 2); maxZ = Math.min(maxZ, HF_EXTENT - 2);
      const NI = Math.floor((maxX - minX) / C) + 1, NJ = Math.floor((maxZ - minZ) / C) + 1;
      const level = new Float32Array(NI * NJ).fill(NaN);
      const ground = new Float32Array(NI * NJ);
      const fdx = new Float32Array(NI * NJ), fdz = new Float32Array(NI * NJ), fsp = new Float32Array(NI * NJ), flake = new Float32Array(NI * NJ);
      const edgeR = Math.min(TERRAIN_RADIUS - 4, 400);
      for (let j = 0; j < NJ; j++) {
        const z = minZ + j * C;
        for (let i = 0; i < NI; i++) {
          const x = minX + i * C, q = j * NI + i;
          const g = sampleHeight(x, z);
          ground[q] = g;
          if (Math.hypot(x, z) > edgeR) continue;
          let w = null, lake = 0;
          if (inLakeBody(x, z) && g < LAKE.level) { w = LAKE.level; lake = 1; }
          const p = riverProject(x, z);
          if (p.d < RIVER_CORR) {
            const surf = riverSurfAt(p.s);
            if (g < surf && (w === null || surf > w + 0.001)) { w = surf; lake = 0; }
            if (g < surf || w !== null) {
              const sp = riverSpeedAt(p.s) * smoothstep01(1 - p.d / (RIVER_CORR * 0.9));
              if (sp > 0.01) {
                const [dx, dz] = riverFlowDir(p.s);
                fdx[q] = dx; fdz[q] = dz; fsp[q] = sp;
                lake = Math.min(lake, 1 - smoothstep01(sp / 0.5));
              }
            }
          }
          if (w === null) continue;
          level[q] = w; flake[q] = lake;
        }
      }
      // Vertices: every node of any cell that has a wet corner. A dry node takes the
      // highest level among its wet neighbours, so the sheet carries on flat under the
      // bank rather than dipping to meet the ground.
      const vIndex = new Int32Array(NI * NJ).fill(-1);
      const pos = [], dep = [], flow = [], idx = [];
      const vert = (i, j) => {
        const q = j * NI + i;
        if (vIndex[q] >= 0) return vIndex[q];
        let w = level[q], lake = flake[q], dx = fdx[q], dz = fdz[q], sp = fsp[q];
        if (Number.isNaN(w)) {
          w = -Infinity;
          for (let dj = -1; dj <= 1; dj++) for (let di = -1; di <= 1; di++) {
            const ii = i + di, jj = j + dj;
            if (ii < 0 || jj < 0 || ii >= NI || jj >= NJ) continue;
            const qq = jj * NI + ii;
            if (!Number.isNaN(level[qq]) && level[qq] > w) { w = level[qq]; lake = flake[qq]; dx = fdx[qq]; dz = fdz[qq]; sp = fsp[qq] * 0.5; }
          }
        }
        vIndex[q] = pos.length / 3;
        pos.push(minX + i * C, w, minZ + j * C);
        dep.push(w - ground[q]);
        flow.push(dx, dz, sp, lake);
        return vIndex[q];
      };
      for (let j = 0; j < NJ - 1; j++) for (let i = 0; i < NI - 1; i++) {
        const q = j * NI + i;
        if (Number.isNaN(level[q]) && Number.isNaN(level[q + 1]) && Number.isNaN(level[q + NI]) && Number.isNaN(level[q + NI + 1])) continue;
        const a = vert(i, j), b = vert(i + 1, j), c = vert(i + 1, j + 1), d = vert(i, j + 1);
        // Wound to face up.
        idx.push(a, c, b, a, d, c);
      }
      if (!idx.length) return;
      const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
      geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(pos, 3));
      geo.setAttribute('wdepth', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(dep, 1));
      geo.setAttribute('wflow', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(flow, 4));
      // Baked colour and alpha for the fallback material (and anything that reads
      // vertex colour): the same depth ramp the shader uses, without the movement.
      const col = new Float32Array((pos.length / 3) * 4);
      for (let v = 0; v < pos.length / 3; v++) {
        const c4 = waterColourAt(dep[v], 0.5, 0, flow[v * 4 + 2], 0.25);
        col[v * 4] = c4[0]; col[v * 4 + 1] = c4[1]; col[v * 4 + 2] = c4[2]; col[v * 4 + 3] = c4[3];
      }
      geo.setAttribute('color', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(col, 4));
      geo.setIndex(idx);
      const nrm = new Float32Array(pos.length); for (let v = 0; v < pos.length / 3; v++) nrm[v * 3 + 1] = 1;
      geo.setAttribute('normal', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(nrm, 3));
      geo.computeBoundingSphere();
      const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, waterFallbackMat);
      mesh.renderOrder = 2;
      mesh.frustumCulled = false;
      mesh.userData.water = true;
      streamGroup.add(mesh);
      const target = { mesh, base: Float32Array.from(pos), depth: Float32Array.from(dep), lake: Float32Array.from(flow.filter((_, k) => k % 4 === 3)), gpu: false };
      waterSurfaceTargets.push(target);
      try {
        if (!WATER_FORCE_CPU) { mesh.material = buildWaterSurfaceMaterial(); target.gpu = true; waterOnGPU = true; }
      } catch (err) {
        console.warn('Grave Shift: water shader failed to build, using the plain surface.', err);
        mesh.material = waterFallbackMat; target.gpu = false;
      }
      mesh.material.userData.water = true;
    }

    // The water's colour and alpha for a depth, a surface pattern value (0..1), a view
    // term (0 looking straight down .. 1 grazing), a current speed, and the foam
    // pattern — shared by the fallback bake and the preview renderer, and written out
    // again below as the shader, term for term.
    function waterColourAt(depth, rip, fres, speed, foamN, lap = 0.5) {
      const T = WATER_TINT;
      const dk = smoothstep01((depth - 0.1) / 1.3), dk2 = smoothstep01((depth - 1.4) / 2.6);
      let r = T.shallow[0] + (T.mid[0] - T.shallow[0]) * dk, g = T.shallow[1] + (T.mid[1] - T.shallow[1]) * dk, b = T.shallow[2] + (T.mid[2] - T.shallow[2]) * dk;
      r += (T.deep[0] - r) * dk2; g += (T.deep[1] - g) * dk2; b += (T.deep[2] - b) * dk2;
      const sk = fres * 0.5 + 0.06;
      r += (T.sky[0] - r) * sk; g += (T.sky[1] - g) * sk; b += (T.sky[2] - b) * sk;
      const lit = 0.83 + rip * 0.34;
      r *= lit; g *= lit; b *= lit;
      const glint = smoothstep01((rip - 0.74) / 0.18) * 0.16;
      r += glint; g += glint; b += glint;
      // Foam: a lapping line at the shore, and broken streaks where the river runs fast
      // over shallow water.
      const shore = (1 - smoothstep01(depth / 0.22)) * smoothstep01((depth + 0.06) / 0.08);
      const foamShore = shore * smoothstep01((foamN * 0.6 + lap * 0.4 - 0.38) / 0.34);
      const runs = smoothstep01((speed - 0.55) / 0.8) * (0.35 + 0.65 * (1 - smoothstep01((depth - 0.2) / 0.7)));
      const foamRiver = runs * smoothstep01((rip - 0.6) / 0.25);
      const f = Math.min(1, foamShore * 0.85 + foamRiver * 0.6);
      r += (T.foam[0] - r) * f * 0.75; g += (T.foam[1] - g) * f * 0.75; b += (T.foam[2] - b) * f * 0.75;
      const edge = smoothstep01((depth + 0.02) / 0.16);
      const a = Math.min(0.93, ((0.32 + (0.8 - 0.32) * smoothstep01((depth - 0.05) / 1.95)) + f * 0.35 + fres * 0.12) * edge);
      return [r, g, b, a];
    }

    const waterFallbackMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
      color: 0xffffff, vertexColors: true, roughness: 0.5, metalness: 0,
      transparent: true, depthWrite: false
    });

    function buildWaterSurfaceMaterial() {
      const { uniform, attribute, vec2, vec3, float, sin, mix, smoothstep, min, abs, clamp, normalize, fract, pow, texture, positionLocal, positionWorld, cameraPosition } = TSL;
      if (!waterTimeUniform) waterTimeUniform = uniform(0);
      const t = waterTimeUniform;
      const P = positionLocal;
      const depth = attribute('wdepth', 'float');
      const fl = attribute('wflow', 'vec4');
      const dir = vec2(fl.x, fl.y), speed = fl.z, lake = fl.w;
      // A slight swell on the open lake, a shiver on the river, none where it shallows
      // to the bank (so the edge never lifts off the ground).
      const amp = smoothstep(0.05, 0.8, depth).mul(lake.mul(0.04).add(0.01));
      const swell = sin(P.x.mul(0.23).add(P.z.mul(0.11)).add(t.mul(0.9))).mul(0.6)
        .add(sin(P.x.mul(-0.09).add(P.z.mul(0.31)).add(t.mul(1.3))).mul(0.4))
        .add(sin(P.x.mul(0.53).sub(P.z.mul(0.47)).add(t.mul(2.1))).mul(0.25));
      const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardNodeMaterial({ roughness: 0.46, metalness: 0, transparent: true, depthWrite: false });
      mat.positionNode = vec3(P.x, P.y.add(swell.mul(amp)), P.z);
      const xz = vec2(positionWorld.x, positionWorld.z);
      // Lake: two layers of pattern drifting past each other.
      const la = texture(waterNoiseTex, xz.mul(0.045).add(vec2(t.mul(0.011), t.mul(0.007)))).r;
      const lb = texture(waterNoiseTex, xz.mul(0.083).add(vec2(t.mul(-0.009), t.mul(0.013)))).g;
      const lakeRip = la.mul(0.6).add(lb.mul(0.4));
      // River: the pattern is carried downstream at the current's speed. Two copies a
      // half-cycle apart, each reset in turn while the other carries the look, so it
      // flows forever without smearing out.
      const period = 2.6;
      const ph0 = fract(t.div(period)), ph1 = fract(t.div(period).add(0.5));
      const w0 = float(1).sub(abs(ph0.mul(2).sub(1)));
      const travel = speed.mul(period);
      const r0 = texture(waterNoiseTex, xz.sub(dir.mul(travel.mul(ph0))).mul(0.085)).b;
      const r1 = texture(waterNoiseTex, xz.sub(dir.mul(travel.mul(ph1))).mul(0.085).add(vec2(0.37, 0.61))).b;
      const rs0 = texture(waterNoiseTex, xz.sub(dir.mul(travel.mul(ph0))).mul(0.21)).r;
      const rs1 = texture(waterNoiseTex, xz.sub(dir.mul(travel.mul(ph1))).mul(0.21).add(vec2(0.21, 0.83))).r;
      const riverRip = mix(r1.mul(0.6).add(rs1.mul(0.4)), r0.mul(0.6).add(rs0.mul(0.4)), w0);
      const running = smoothstep(0.05, 0.3, speed);
      const rip = mix(lakeRip, riverRip, running);
      // Depth: pale and clear over the shallows, blue with depth.
      const TW = WATER_TINT, v3 = (a) => vec3(a[0], a[1], a[2]);
      const dk = smoothstep(0.1, 1.4, depth), dk2 = smoothstep(1.4, 4.0, depth);
      let col = mix(mix(v3(TW.shallow), v3(TW.mid), dk), v3(TW.deep), dk2);
      // The sky in it, more as the view flattens out across it.
      const V = normalize(cameraPosition.sub(positionWorld));
      const fres = pow(float(1).sub(clamp(V.y, 0, 1)), 4.0);
      col = mix(col, v3(TW.sky), fres.mul(0.5).add(0.06));
      col = col.mul(rip.mul(0.34).add(0.83)).add(smoothstep(0.74, 0.92, rip).mul(0.16));
      // Foam.
      const lap = sin(t.mul(1.1).add(la.mul(9.0))).mul(0.5).add(0.5);
      const shore = float(1).sub(smoothstep(0.0, 0.22, depth)).mul(smoothstep(-0.06, 0.02, depth));
      const foamShore = shore.mul(smoothstep(0.38, 0.72, lb.mul(0.6).add(lap.mul(0.4))));
      const runs = smoothstep(0.55, 1.35, speed).mul(float(1).sub(smoothstep(0.2, 0.9, depth)).mul(0.65).add(0.35));
      const foamRiver = runs.mul(smoothstep(0.6, 0.85, rip));
      const f = min(foamShore.mul(0.85).add(foamRiver.mul(0.6)), 1.0);
      col = mix(col, v3(TW.foam), f.mul(0.75));
      mat.colorNode = col;
      const edge = smoothstep(-0.02, 0.14, depth);
      const alpha = mix(0.32, 0.8, smoothstep(0.05, 2.0, depth)).add(f.mul(0.35)).add(fres.mul(0.12)).mul(edge);
      mat.opacityNode = min(alpha, 0.93);
      return mat;
    }

    function scatterStreamPebbles() {
      const rnd = mulberry32(0x5eab17);
      const pts = buildRiverStations(7);
      // River stone is sorted and worn, not one grey lump repeated: a handful of tints
      // for the bar, and a pool of roughened shapes so no two stones share a profile.
      // Geometry and materials are pooled rather than made per stone — these are
      // separate meshes, so every extra material is another batch.
      const pebbleMats = [
        new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x8a9098, roughness: 0.82, metalness: 0.05 }),
        new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x6f7680, roughness: 0.86, metalness: 0.05 }),
        new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x9c8e79, roughness: 0.88, metalness: 0.04 }),
        new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xa8a9a2, roughness: 0.78, metalness: 0.06 })
      ];
      const geos = [];
      for (let k = 0; k < 9; k++) {
        const r = 0.11 + (k % 3) * 0.07 + (k / 9) * 0.06;
        const g = k % 3 === 2
          ? new THREE.IcosahedronGeometry(r, 0)
          : new THREE.DodecahedronGeometry(r, 0);
        // Tumbled smooth, so the noise is gentle compared with a hillside boulder.
        geos.push(roughenStone(g, 0.16, 0x5eab17 + k * 37));
      }
      for (let i = 1; i < pts.length - 1; i++) {
        if (rnd() < 0.28) continue;
        const p = pts[i];
        // Stones gather in bars of two or three, not one per station.
        const n = 1 + ((rnd() * 3) | 0);
        for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
          const side = rnd() < 0.5 ? 1 : -1;
          const off = RIVER_WIDTH * (0.9 + rnd() * 0.5);
          const along = (rnd() - 0.5) * 1.6;
          const bx = p.x + p.nx * side * off + p.nz * along;
          const bz = p.z + p.nz * side * off - p.nx * along;
          // Stop short of LAND_MAX rather than at it: that is where the boundary wall's
          // inner face stands, and a pebble sitting on the line pokes through the stone.
          // (Written as a literal because this runs before the wall constants exist.)
          if (Math.hypot(bx, bz) > LAND_MAX - 1.5) continue;
          if (inLakeBody(bx, bz) && sampleHeight(bx, bz) < LAKE.level + 0.2) continue;
          const peb = new THREE.Mesh(
            geos[(i * 3 + k) % geos.length],
            pebbleMats[(rnd() * pebbleMats.length) | 0]
          );
          peb.position.set(bx, sampleHeight(bx, bz) - 0.04, bz);
          peb.rotation.set(rnd() * 3, rnd() * 3, rnd() * 3);
          // Worn flat by the water and bedded into the bar, with the odd bigger cobble.
          const sc = rnd() < 0.12 ? 1.5 + rnd() * 0.8 : 0.55 + rnd() * 0.8;
          peb.scale.set(sc, sc * (0.55 + rnd() * 0.35), sc);
          peb.castShadow = true;
          peb.receiveShadow = true;
          streamGroup.add(peb);
        }
      }
    }

    // The level water stands at near a point, wet or dry — for placing things at the
    // water's edge (a dry point just above the lake still "belongs" to the lake).
    function waterPotentialLevel(x, z) {
      let w = null;
      if (lakeDist(x, z) < LAKE_REACH - 4) w = LAKE.level;
      const p = riverProject(x, z);
      if (p.d < RIVER_CORR + 3) { const s = riverSurfAt(p.s); if (w === null || s > w) w = s; }
      return w;
    }
    // Current speed at a point (0 on the lake and on dry land).
    function waterCurrentAt(x, z) {
      const p = riverProject(x, z);
      if (p.d > RIVER_CORR) return 0;
      return riverSpeedAt(p.s) * smoothstep01(1 - p.d / (RIVER_CORR * 0.9));
    }

    // === Life in and around the water =============================================
    // Reeds and cattails standing in the margins, weed rising off the bed, stones and
    // cobbles on it, lily pads drifting in the calm shallows of the lake, and ferns,
    // long grass and flowers along the banks. Everything is merged into a handful of
    // meshes per patch of shore, so it costs a few draw calls, not thousands.
    function scatterWaterLife() {
      const rnd = mulberry32(0x9eed5);
      // Sample the whole water region on a 1.1m grid once; everything below picks from
      // these spots.
      const spots = [];
      const C = 1.1;
      let minX = LAKE.x - LAKE_REACH, maxX = LAKE.x + LAKE_REACH, minZ = LAKE.z - LAKE_REACH, maxZ = LAKE.z + LAKE_REACH;
      for (const c of RIVER_CTRL) { minX = Math.min(minX, c.x - 16); maxX = Math.max(maxX, c.x + 16); minZ = Math.min(minZ, c.z - 16); maxZ = Math.max(maxZ, c.z + 16); }
      for (let z = minZ; z <= maxZ; z += C) for (let x = minX; x <= maxX; x += C) {
        if (Math.hypot(x, z) > LAND_MAX - 3) continue;
        const jx = x + (rnd() - 0.5) * C * 0.9, jz = z + (rnd() - 0.5) * C * 0.9;
        const lvl = waterPotentialLevel(jx, jz);
        if (lvl === null) continue;
        const g = sampleHeight(jx, jz);
        const d = lvl - g;                       // depth (negative = that far above the water)
        if (d < -1.2) continue;
        if (nearPOI(jx, jz, 3) || distToPath(jx, jz) < 1.2) continue;
        spots.push({ x: jx, z: jz, g, lvl, d, cur: waterCurrentAt(jx, jz) });
      }
      // Clumping: life grows in patches, not evenly.
      const patch = (x, z, f, seed) => fbm(x * f + seed, z * f - seed * 0.7, 2);

      // Patches of shore get their own meshes so wind can lean each about its own middle.
      const CHUNK = 36;
      const chunks = new Map();
      const chunkFor = (x, z) => {
        const key = Math.floor(x / CHUNK) + ',' + Math.floor(z / CHUNK);
        let ch = chunks.get(key);
        if (!ch) { ch = { cx: (Math.floor(x / CHUNK) + 0.5) * CHUNK, cz: (Math.floor(z / CHUNK) + 0.5) * CHUNK, reeds: makeAcc(), weed: makeAcc(), pads: makeAcc() }; chunks.set(key, ch); }
        return ch;
      };
      const tri = (acc, ch, A, B, Cc, col) => {
        let nx = (B[1] - A[1]) * (Cc[2] - A[2]) - (B[2] - A[2]) * (Cc[1] - A[1]);
        let ny = (B[2] - A[2]) * (Cc[0] - A[0]) - (B[0] - A[0]) * (Cc[2] - A[2]);
        let nz = (B[0] - A[0]) * (Cc[1] - A[1]) - (B[1] - A[1]) * (Cc[0] - A[0]);
        const l = Math.hypot(nx, ny, nz) || 1; nx /= l; ny /= l; nz /= l;
        if (ny < 0) { nx = -nx; ny = -ny; nz = -nz; }
        for (let k = 0; k < 3; k++) { const P = [A, B, Cc][k], c = col[k] || col[0]; accVert(acc, P[0] - ch.cx, P[1], P[2] - ch.cz, nx, ny, nz, c[0], c[1], c[2]); }
      };
      const _c = new THREE.Color(), _c2 = new THREE.Color();
      const rgb = (hex, v = 0) => { _c.set(hex).multiplyScalar(1 + v); return [_c.r, _c.g, _c.b]; };
      // A tapered blade from the base, leaning, bending, tip paler.
      const blade = (acc, ch, x, y, z, h, w, lean, dirA, baseHex, tipHex) => {
        const segs = 3, dx = Math.cos(dirA), dz = Math.sin(dirA), px = -dz, pz = dx;
        let prevL = null, prevR = null;
        for (let s = 0; s <= segs; s++) {
          const u = s / segs, bend = lean * u * u;
          const cx = x + dx * bend * h, cz = z + dz * bend * h, cy = y + h * u * (1 - lean * u * 0.25);
          const ww = w * (1 - u * 0.85);
          const L = [cx + px * ww, cy, cz + pz * ww], R = [cx - px * ww, cy, cz - pz * ww];
          _c2.set(baseHex).lerp(_c.set(tipHex), u);
          const c = [_c2.r, _c2.g, _c2.b];
          if (prevL) { tri(acc, ch, prevL, prevR, R, [c]); tri(acc, ch, prevL, R, L, [c]); }
          prevL = L; prevR = R;
        }
      };

      // --- Reeds and cattails in the margins ---
      let reeds = 0;
      for (const s of spots) {
        if (s.d < -0.35 || s.d > 0.65 || s.cur > 1.1) continue;
        const pk = patch(s.x, s.z, 0.07, 3.1);
        if (pk < 0.02 || rnd() > 0.55 * smoothstep01((pk - 0.02) / 0.25)) continue;
        const ch = chunkFor(s.x, s.z);
        const n = 5 + Math.floor(rnd() * 8);
        const tall = 1.2 + rnd() * 0.9;
        for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
          const a = rnd() * 6.28, r = rnd() * 0.35;
          const bx = s.x + Math.cos(a) * r, bz = s.z + Math.sin(a) * r;
          const by = sampleHeight(bx, bz) - 0.05;
          const h = tall * (0.6 + rnd() * 0.5);
          const hue = rnd();
          blade(ch.reeds, ch, bx, by, bz, h, 0.022 + rnd() * 0.012, 0.18 + rnd() * 0.3, rnd() * 6.28,
            hue < 0.5 ? 0x4d6a2c : 0x5d7a34, hue < 0.7 ? 0x9aa45a : 0xb7a866);
          // Some of them carry a cattail head.
          if (k < 2 && rnd() < 0.35) {
            const hx = bx, hz = bz, hy = by + h * 0.92, hr = 0.03;
            const brown = rgb(0x5a3c22, (rnd() - 0.5) * 0.2);
            for (let q = 0; q < 4; q++) {
              const a0 = q / 4 * 6.28, a1 = (q + 1) / 4 * 6.28;
              const P0 = [hx + Math.cos(a0) * hr, hy, hz + Math.sin(a0) * hr], P1 = [hx + Math.cos(a1) * hr, hy, hz + Math.sin(a1) * hr];
              const Q0 = [P0[0], hy + 0.2, P0[2]], Q1 = [P1[0], hy + 0.2, P1[2]];
              tri(ch.reeds, ch, P0, P1, Q1, [brown]); tri(ch.reeds, ch, P0, Q1, Q0, [brown]);
            }
          }
        }
        reeds++;
      }

      // --- Weed rising off the bed ---
      for (const s of spots) {
        if (s.d < 0.45 || s.d > 2.8 || s.cur > 1.25) continue;
        const pk = patch(s.x, s.z, 0.05, 11.7);
        if (pk < 0.05 || rnd() > 0.24 * smoothstep01((pk - 0.05) / 0.3)) continue;
        const ch = chunkFor(s.x, s.z);
        const n = 4 + Math.floor(rnd() * 5);
        // Weed in a current streams downstream; in the lake it stands and leans a little.
        let fx = 0, fz = 0;
        if (s.cur > 0.05) { const p = riverProject(s.x, s.z); [fx, fz] = riverFlowDir(p.s); }
        for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
          const a = rnd() * 6.28, r = rnd() * 0.45;
          const bx = s.x + Math.cos(a) * r, bz = s.z + Math.sin(a) * r;
          const by = sampleHeight(bx, bz) - 0.03;
          const h = (s.lvl - by) * (0.45 + rnd() * 0.45);
          const dirA = s.cur > 0.05 ? Math.atan2(fz, fx) + (rnd() - 0.5) * 0.4 : rnd() * 6.28;
          const lean = s.cur > 0.05 ? 0.55 + s.cur * 0.35 : 0.12 + rnd() * 0.25;
          blade(ch.weed, ch, bx, by, bz, h, 0.035 + rnd() * 0.03, lean, dirA, 0x243d1d, rnd() < 0.5 ? 0x4f6b2a : 0x5f7a33);
        }
      }

      // --- Lily pads in the calm, shallow lake ---
      for (const s of spots) {
        if (s.d < 0.35 || s.d > 1.6 || s.cur > 0.02 || s.lvl !== LAKE.level) continue;
        const pk = patch(s.x, s.z, 0.045, 27.3);
        if (pk < 0.18 || rnd() > 0.2 * smoothstep01((pk - 0.18) / 0.2)) continue;
        const ch = chunkFor(s.x, s.z);
        const n = 3 + Math.floor(rnd() * 6);
        for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) {
          const a = rnd() * 6.28, r = rnd() * 1.1;
          const px = s.x + Math.cos(a) * r, pz = s.z + Math.sin(a) * r;
          if (waterDepthAt(px, pz) < 0.25) continue;
          const R = 0.22 + rnd() * 0.22, y = LAKE.level + 0.045, rot = rnd() * 6.28, notch = 0.55;
          const green = rgb(rnd() < 0.5 ? 0x2f6b34 : 0x3e7b3a, (rnd() - 0.5) * 0.25);
          const rim = rgb(0x4d6b2c);
          const segs = 10;
          for (let q = 0; q < segs; q++) {
            const a0 = rot + notch / 2 + (q / segs) * (6.28 - notch), a1 = rot + notch / 2 + ((q + 1) / segs) * (6.28 - notch);
            tri(ch.pads, ch, [px, y + 0.01, pz], [px + Math.cos(a0) * R, y, pz + Math.sin(a0) * R], [px + Math.cos(a1) * R, y, pz + Math.sin(a1) * R], [green, rim, rim]);
          }
          if (rnd() < 0.12) {
            const fcol = rgb(rnd() < 0.6 ? 0xf3eaf2 : 0xf2b7cf), core = rgb(0xf2d25a);
            for (let q = 0; q < 6; q++) {
              const a0 = q / 6 * 6.28, fx = px + Math.cos(rot) * R * 0.2, fz = pz + Math.sin(rot) * R * 0.2;
              tri(ch.pads, ch, [fx, y + 0.02, fz], [fx + Math.cos(a0 - 0.3) * 0.08, y + 0.07, fz + Math.sin(a0 - 0.3) * 0.08], [fx + Math.cos(a0 + 0.3) * 0.08, y + 0.07, fz + Math.sin(a0 + 0.3) * 0.08], [core, fcol, fcol]);
            }
          }
        }
      }

      // --- Stones on the beds, and cobbles down the river ---
      caveMaterials();
      const stoneAcc = makeAcc();
      const bedDesign = { rock: 0x6d6a62, dark: 0x3f3d37, moss: 0x4f6630 };
      const riverDesign = { rock: 0x7b7b74, dark: 0x4a4944, moss: 0x5a6a36 };
      let stones = 0;
      for (const s of spots) {
        if (s.d < -0.3 || s.d > 2.2) continue;
        const inRiver = s.cur > 0.1;
        const pk = patch(s.x, s.z, 0.09, 41.9);
        const want = inRiver ? 0.12 : 0.05 * smoothstep01((pk + 0.1) / 0.3);
        if (rnd() > want) continue;
        const big = rnd() < 0.12;
        const r = big ? 0.45 + rnd() * 0.5 : 0.1 + rnd() * 0.22;
        const y = sampleHeight(s.x, s.z);
        addBoulder(stoneAcc, inRiver ? riverDesign : bedDesign, s.x, y + r * 0.1, s.z, r * (1 + rnd() * 0.3), r * (0.5 + rnd() * 0.25), r * (1 + rnd() * 0.3), 7 + stones * 3.3, { floor: y, lump: 0.35, moss: s.d > 0.1 ? 0.9 : 0.4 });
        stones++;
      }
      if (stoneAcc.p.length) {
        const m = new THREE.Mesh(accToGeometry(stoneAcc), caveRockMat);
        m.receiveShadow = true; m.castShadow = true;
        m.userData.bedLife = true;
        scene.add(m);
      }

      // Meshes: reeds lean in the wind, weed and pads do not.
      const reedMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ vertexColors: true, roughness: 0.9, side: THREE.DoubleSide });
      const weedMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ vertexColors: true, roughness: 0.95, side: THREE.DoubleSide });
      const padMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ vertexColors: true, roughness: 0.7, side: THREE.DoubleSide });
      for (const ch of chunks.values()) {
        for (const [acc, mat, sway] of [[ch.reeds, reedMat, 0.05], [ch.weed, weedMat, 0], [ch.pads, padMat, 0]]) {
          if (!acc.p.length) continue;
          const m = new THREE.Mesh(accToGeometry(acc), mat);
          m.position.set(ch.cx, 0, ch.cz);
          m.userData.bedLife = true;
          m.castShadow = acc === ch.reeds;
          scene.add(m);
          if (sway) windSwayables.push({ mesh: m, phase: rnd() * 6.28, amount: sway });
        }
      }

      // --- The banks: ferns, long grass and flowers down to the water ---
      for (const s of spots) {
        if (s.d > -0.12 || s.d < -1.2) continue;
        if (terrainSlope(s.x, s.z) > 0.55) continue;
        const r = rnd();
        if (r < 0.1) makeFern(s.x, s.z, rnd);
        else if (r < 0.22) makeGrassTuft(s.x, s.z, rnd, 0.9);
        else if (r < 0.245 && s.cur < 0.05) makeFlowerCluster(s.x, s.z, rnd);
      }
      // And nothing left standing in water that has no business there.
      for (let i = foliage.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        const f = foliage[i];
        if (waterDepthAt(f.x, f.z) > 0.04) {
          if (f.mesh) scene.remove(f.mesh);
          const w = windSwayables.findIndex((q) => q.mesh === f.mesh);
          if (w >= 0) windSwayables.splice(w, 1);
          foliage.splice(i, 1);
        }
      }
      for (let i = trees.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        const t = trees[i];
        if (waterDepthAt(t.x, t.z) > 0.15) { scene.remove(t.group); trees.splice(i, 1); }
      }
      return { reeds, stones, chunks: chunks.size };
    }

    buildWaterSurface();
    scatterStreamPebbles();
    // scatterReeds() runs later — it needs the prop-merging helpers.

    // === POI construction ===
    // Meshes for the landmarks planned above. Each landmark merges into a handful of
    // draw calls and registers its own colliders.
    const poiMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ vertexColors: true, roughness: 0.85 });
    const emberGlowMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
      color: 0xff5a1a, emissive: 0xff6a22, emissiveIntensity: 1.4, roughness: 0.8
    });

    function poiBox(parts, mat, w, h, d, x, y, z, ry = 0, rz = 0, rx = 0) {
      const m = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d), mat);
      m.position.set(x, y, z);
      m.rotation.set(rx, ry, rz);
      parts.push(m);
      return m;
    }

    function appendLandmarkDetails(parts, kind, cx, cz, gy, yaw = 0, options = {}) {
      const c = Math.cos(yaw), s = Math.sin(yaw);
      const details = window.buildLandmarkDetails(THREE, { kind, ...options,
        ground: (x, z) => sampleHeight(cx + x * c + z * s, cz - x * s + z * c) - gy });
      if (options.bakeYaw) {
        const rotation = new THREE.Matrix4().makeRotationY(yaw);
        for (const part of details.parts) part.applyMatrix4(rotation);
      }
      parts.push(...details.parts);
      return { theme: details.theme, register(owner = null) {
        for (const p of details.solids) {
          const collider = addSolid(cx + p.x * c + p.z * s, cz - p.x * s + p.z * c,
            p.r, gy + p.y, gy + p.y + p.h, owner);
          if (owner) owner.colliders.push(collider);
        }
      } };
    }

    // Highest ground under a strip running along local z from -halfLen*t.. — sampled
    // across the width too (not just the centreline) — so a bump anywhere under the
    // deck, not only at its two sampled ends, still gets found.
    function crestAcrossStrip(cx, cz, yaw, halfLen, halfWidth) {
      const cy = Math.cos(yaw), sy = Math.sin(yaw);
      let crest = -Infinity;
      for (let t = -1; t <= 1.0001; t += 0.03) {
        const lz = t * halfLen;
        for (const w of [-1, 0, 1]) {
          const lx = w * (halfWidth - 0.1);
          crest = Math.max(crest, sampleHeight(cx + Math.sin(yaw) * lz + lx * cy, cz + Math.cos(yaw) * lz - lx * sy));
        }
      }
      return crest;
    }

    // Bank height at one end of a crossing, sampled across the full width (not just
    // the centreline) so a shoreline that isn't flat side-to-side doesn't leave one
    // edge of the approach still gapped or clipping while the other looks fine.
    function bankHeightAcross(cx, cz, yaw, halfWidth) {
      const cy = Math.cos(yaw), sy = Math.sin(yaw);
      let m = sampleHeight(cx, cz);
      for (const w of [-1, 1]) {
        const lx = w * (halfWidth - 0.1);
        m = Math.max(m, sampleHeight(cx + lx * cy, cz - lx * sy));
      }
      return m;
    }

    function buildCampsite(cx, cz, seed) {
      const rnd = mulberry32(seed);
      // Seat at centre ground; each tent then levels onto its own patch, so the small
      // clutter around the fire doesn't sink on sloped sites.
      const gy = sampleHeight(cx, cz) - 0.04;
      const lm = {
        kind: 'campsite', x: cx, z: cz, gy, hp: CAMPSITE_MAX_HP, maxHp: CAMPSITE_MAX_HP, alive: true,
        mesh: null, colliders: [], debrisColor: 0x8c7a4f, rubbleRadius: 3.0
      };
      const siteIndex = POI.campsites.findIndex(c => c.x === cx && c.z === cz);
      const details = window.buildCampsiteDetails(THREE, {
        cx, cz, gy, variant: (siteIndex < 0 ? Math.abs(seed) : siteIndex) % 3,
        random: rnd, height: sampleHeight,
        solid: (x, z, radius, y0, y1) => lm.colliders.push(addSolid(x, z, radius, y0, y1, lm))
      });
      const parts = details.parts;
      const story = appendLandmarkDetails(parts, 'camp', cx, cz, gy, details.yaw,
        { variant: (siteIndex < 0 ? Math.abs(seed) : siteIndex) % 3, bakeYaw: true });
      story.register(lm);
      lm.campStyle = details.style;
      if (siteIndex >= 0) POI.campsites[siteIndex].style = details.style;
      lm.campYaw = details.yaw;
      const mesh = mergeParts(parts, poiMat, { castShadow: true, receiveShadow: true });
      for (const part of parts) part.geometry.dispose();
      for (const material of details.materials) material.dispose();
      mesh.position.set(cx, gy, cz);
      scene.add(mesh);
      lm.mesh = mesh;

      mesh.userData.landmarkTheme = story.theme;

      // Embers + firelight.
      const ember = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(0.3, 0.34, 6), emberGlowMat);
      ember.position.set(cx, gy + 0.2, cz);
      scene.add(ember);
      lm.emberMesh = ember;
      const light = new THREE.PointLight(0xff8c3a, 0, 11, 2);
      light.position.set(cx, gy + 1.0, cz);
      scene.add(light);
      lm.light = light;
      const cf = { x: cx, z: cz, y: gy, light, phase: rnd() * 9 };
      campfires.push(cf);
      lm.campfire = cf;

      landmarks.push(lm);
      return lm;
    }

    function buildCabin(cx, cz, seed) {
      const rnd = mulberry32(seed);
      const gy = groundMinAround(cx, cz, 1.6) - 0.06;
      const yaw = rnd() * Math.PI * 2;
      const parts = [];
      const plank = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x77573a });
      const plankOld = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x5c4630 });
      const stone = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x6f6d68 });

      // The ruined floorboards follow the local ground in landmark-details.js.
      poiBox(parts, plank, 5.0, 2.0, 0.24, 0, 1.14, -1.9);                 // back wall
      poiBox(parts, plank, 0.24, 2.0, 3.9, -2.4, 1.14, 0);                 // left wall
      poiBox(parts, plankOld, 0.24, 1.2, 1.4, 2.4, 0.74, -1.2);            // right stub
      poiBox(parts, plankOld, 0.24, 0.8, 1.0, 2.4, 0.54, 1.3);             // right stub 2
      // Collapsed roof: one panel still leaning, planks spilled inside.
      poiBox(parts, plankOld, 3.4, 0.14, 3.0, -0.9, 2.15, -0.6, 0, 0.42);
      for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        poiBox(parts, rnd() < 0.5 ? plank : plankOld, 0.34, 0.1, 2.6 + rnd(), 0.6 + rnd() * 1.2, 0.45 + i * 0.1, rnd() - 0.5, rnd() * 2, 0, rnd() * 0.4);
      }
      const chim = poiBox(parts, stone, 0.72, 2.9, 0.72, 1.7, 1.45, -1.5);
      poiBox(parts, stone, 0.9, 0.3, 0.9, 1.7, 0.15, -1.5);

      const details = appendLandmarkDetails(parts, 'cabin', cx, cz, gy, yaw,
        { variant: POI.cabins.findIndex(p => p.x === cx && p.z === cz) });

      const g = new THREE.Group();
      const mesh = mergeParts(parts, poiMat, { castShadow: true, receiveShadow: true });
      g.add(mesh);
      g.position.set(cx, gy, cz);
      g.rotation.y = yaw;
      scene.add(g);

      const lm = {
        kind: 'cabin', x: cx, z: cz, gy, hp: CABIN_MAX_HP, maxHp: CABIN_MAX_HP, alive: true,
        mesh: g, colliders: [], debrisColor: 0x6b5539, rubbleRadius: 2.1
      };

      // Colliders, rotated into world space.
      const cy = Math.cos(yaw), sy = Math.sin(yaw);
      const w = (lx, lz, r, h) => lm.colliders.push(addSolid(cx + lx * cy + lz * sy, cz - lx * sy + lz * cy, r, gy, gy + h, lm));
      w(-1.6, -1.9, 0.8, 2.2); w(0, -1.9, 0.8, 2.2); w(1.6, -1.9, 0.8, 2.2);   // back wall
      w(-2.4, -1.1, 0.75, 2.2); w(-2.4, 0.9, 0.75, 2.2);                        // left wall
      w(2.4, -1.2, 0.6, 1.6);                                                    // right stub
      w(1.7, -1.5, 0.6, 3.0);                                                    // chimney

      details.register(lm);
      g.userData.landmarkTheme = details.theme;
